info.title: RumptyCloud API
info.description:
The RumptyCloud REST API lets you manage virtual machines, Kubernetes clusters,
databases, storage, deployments and networking programmatically.

bearerAuth.description:
Personal API key created under **Manage Profile → My profile → Personal API keys**,
sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

WorkspaceSlug.name: X-Workspace-Slug
WorkspaceSlug.description: Slug of the workspace the request acts on. You can also pass it as the `workspace_slug` query parameter.

WorkspaceUid.name: workspace_uid
WorkspaceUid.description: The workspace's `uid`. When the route also takes `X-Workspace-Slug`, both must name the same workspace.

WorkspaceMemberUid.name: member_uid
WorkspaceMemberUid.description: The membership's `uid` from [List members](/api/workspaces/list-members). This is not the member's `user_uid`.

WorkspaceInvitationToken.name: token
WorkspaceInvitationToken.description: The secret token from the invitation email link (`/invitations/<token>`).

VmIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
VmIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional unique key for this request, such as a UUID. Leading and trailing spaces are
ignored. If you send a key you already used for the same action on the same resource, the
original operation is returned with `200 OK` and `X-Idempotency-Replay: true`, and nothing
new is queued. The replay check runs before the resource is loaded or its state is
checked, so a retry gets the original result even after the action has finished. Reusing a
key for a different action, resource type or resource returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are shared across the workspace. Without a key,
every request is treated as new.

SnapshotIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
SnapshotIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional unique key for this request, such as a UUID. Leading and trailing spaces are
ignored. If you send a key you already used for the same snapshot action, the original
operation is returned with `200 OK` and `X-Idempotency-Replay: true`, and nothing new is
queued. Reusing a key for a different action or snapshot returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are shared across the workspace. Without a key,
every request is treated as new.

KubernetesIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
KubernetesIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional unique key for this request, such as a UUID. Leading and trailing spaces are
trimmed. If you send a key you already used for the same action on the same cluster, the
original operation is returned with `200 OK`, `is_replay: true` and the
`X-Idempotency-Replay` header, and nothing new is queued. The replay is checked before the
cluster's current state. Reusing a key for a different action or resource returns `409`
with `action: idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are scoped to you and the workspace and shared
by every resource type.

DeploymentIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
DeploymentIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional key that makes retries safe. Repeating a request with a key already used for
the same action on the same deployment returns the original operation with `200 OK` and
`is_replay: true` instead of queuing it again. Reusing it for a different action or
deployment returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

DeploymentActivityDays.name: days
DeploymentActivityDays.description: How many days back to count, up to `366`. Missing, non-numeric, zero, negative or larger values use `365`.

AppIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
AppIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional key that makes retries safe. Repeating a request with a key already used for
the same action returns the original result with `200 OK` and `is_replay: true`. Reusing
it for a different action or app returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

DatabaseIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
DatabaseIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional unique key for this request, such as a UUID. Leading and trailing spaces are
trimmed. If you send a key you already used for the same action on the same resource, the
original operation is returned with `200 OK`, `is_replay: true` and the
`X-Idempotency-Replay` header, and nothing new is queued. The replay is checked before the
resource's current state, so a retry after the first request finished still gets the
original result. Reusing a key for a different action or resource returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are scoped to you and the workspace and shared by
every resource type. Without a key, every request queues a new operation.

DatabaseRedisDb.name: db
DatabaseRedisDb.description: Redis logical database, `0` to `15`. Defaults to `0`. Non-numeric values are treated as `0`.

VolumeIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
VolumeIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional unique key for this request, such as a UUID. Leading and trailing spaces are
trimmed. If the key was already used for the same action (and the same volume, or for a
create the same name), the original operation is returned with `200 OK`,
`is_replay: true` and the `X-Idempotency-Replay` header, and nothing new is queued. The
replay is checked before the volume's current state, so a retry after the first request
finished still gets the original result. If the key was used for any other operation in
the workspace, including VM, database or snapshot operations, the request is rejected with
`409` and `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

BucketIdempotencyKey.name: X-Idempotency
BucketIdempotencyKey.description:
Optional key that makes retries safe. Repeating a request with a key already used for
the same action returns the original operation with `200 OK` and `is_replay: true`
instead of queuing it again. Reusing it for a different action or bucket returns `409`
with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

BucketObjectUid.name: uid
BucketObjectUid.description: The object's `uid` (the `object_id` returned by [Create an upload](/api/buckets/create-an-upload)).

code.description: HTTP status code. Present on most errors, but authentication errors omit it.

action.description: Optional machine-readable hint for the next step, e.g. `past_due` or `account_suspended`.

role.description: Your platform role. This is `user` for customers and is unrelated to your workspace roles.

verified.description: Whether you have verified your email address. Most workspace endpoints return `403` with `action: verify_email` until you have.

auth_method.description: How the account signs in, e.g. `password` or `google`.

avatar_url.description: API-relative path of your profile picture, with a cache-busting `v` parameter. Omitted when you have no picture.

billing_country.description: Country used for tax (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Your declared billing country, or the country detected at signup when you have not set one. Omitted when neither is known.

billing_status.description:
Your payment standing. When it is not `active`, creating new paid resources returns
`402` with `action: past_due`, as do starting VMs and building, redeploying or
restarting deployments. While `suspended`, your VMs, databases, Kubernetes clusters and
deployments are powered off; storage is kept. Once the account is `active` again,
everything suspension powered off is started again automatically within about a
minute (resources you had stopped yourself stay stopped).

cpu_percent.description: CPU usage in percent. Omitted when not recorded.

disk_percent.description: Root filesystem usage in percent. Omitted when not recorded.

network_rx_bytes.description: Bytes received, excluding loopback. Omitted when not recorded.

is_replay.description: `true` when an existing operation was returned for a reused `X-Idempotency` key or an in-flight removal.

is_completed.description: `true` when a returned existing operation has already finished.

stderr_truncated.description: Present and `true` when `stderr` was cut at 64 KiB.

duration_ms.description: How long the command ran, in milliseconds.

vm_uid.description: UID of the VM the snapshot was taken from. Kept after that VM is deleted.

detached.description: `true` when the source VM has been deleted. The snapshot can still be used to create a new VM.

slug.description: URL-safe form of the name.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Only `available` snapshots can be restored or used to create a VM.

consumed_bytes.description: Storage the snapshot actually uses, in bytes. Billing is based on this. `0` until the snapshot is ready.

operation_id.description: UID of the queued operation. Poll it with [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). The snapshot is the operation's `resource_uid`.

vm_uid.description: UID of the VM from the request path. For [Delete a snapshot](/api/snapshots/delete-a-snapshot), the snapshot's source VM, or empty on a replay.

name.description: Name of the VM for VM-scoped requests (empty on a replay if the VM is gone). Name of the snapshot for [Delete a snapshot](/api/snapshots/delete-a-snapshot).

status.description: Status of the operation.

events_url.description: Path of the server-sent events stream with the operation's progress.

is_replay.description: `true` when an existing operation was returned for a reused `X-Idempotency` key.

is_completed.description: `true` when a returned existing operation has already finished.

resource_type.description: Kind of resource the operation acts on, for example `vm`, `vm_app`, `vm_snapshot`, `k8s_cluster`, `volume`, `database` or `deployment`.

resource_uid.description: UID of the resource. For a new VM or snapshot, this is the UID of the resource being created.

resource_name.description: Name of the resource when the operation was queued.

action.description:
What the operation does. For VMs: `create`, `start`, `stop`, `reboot`, `resize`,
`delete`, `set_app_port`, `expose` and `unexpose` (custom domains and apps). For
snapshots: `create`, `restore` and `delete`. Other resources (`k8s_cluster`, `volume`,
`database`, `deployment`, buckets) use `create` and `delete` plus their own actions, for
example `attach_volume`, `detach_volume`, `resize` or `firewall.apply`.

status.description: Progress of the operation. `succeeded` and `failed` are final.

started_at.description: When work began. Omitted while queued.

finished_at.description: When the operation finished. Omitted until it does.

events_url.description: Path of the server-sent events stream with the operation's progress.

slug.description: URL-friendly form of the name, unique among the workspace's clusters.

status.description:
Lifecycle state. `failed` means provisioning or a later action failed. See
`last_failure`. `deleted` is only seen on [Get a cluster](/api/kubernetes/get-a-cluster)
and in idempotent replays.

`stopped` means the platform powered off every node because the account was suspended
for non-payment. A `running` cluster switches to `stopped` (and its nodes to `stopped`,
which ends node billing) as soon as the stop is queued, and stays stopped while the
account is suspended. Within about a minute of the account becoming active again it is
restarted: it goes through `provisioning` back to `running`, or to `failed` if the
restart fails. If the stop itself fails, the cluster goes back to `running` and the stop
is retried. A stopped cluster can still be deleted.

display_status.description: Status to show in user interfaces. Currently always equal to `status`.

version.description: k3s version requested for the cluster.

image_slug.description: Slug of the node operating system image. Omitted if the image cannot be resolved.

endpoint.description: Public Kubernetes API server URL. Omitted when the platform has no Kubernetes domain configured.

kubeconfig.description:
kubeconfig file for the cluster, as YAML text. Omitted until the cluster is running and
the kubeconfig has been retrieved. Never included by [List clusters](/api/kubernetes/list-clusters),
and omitted by [Get a cluster](/api/kubernetes/get-a-cluster) for roles without the
`secrets read` permission. It contains credentials, so store it securely.

last_failure.description: Reason for the last failure reported for the cluster. Omitted when there is none.

nodes.description: The cluster's nodes, the control plane first. Omitted when empty.

name.description: Node name, derived from the cluster name, such as `production-cp-1` or `production-worker-2`.

role.description: Whether the node runs the Kubernetes control plane or workloads.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the node. `stopped` while the cluster is stopped for a suspended account.

plan_slug.description: Compute plan the node runs on.

vcpu.description: Virtual CPUs from the node's plan.

memory_mib.description: Memory from the node's plan, in MiB.

disk_gib.description: Disk included with the node's plan, in GiB.

private_ip.description: Node's private IP address. Omitted until the node is provisioned.

guest_username.description: Operating system user for SSH access to the node.

operation_id.description: UID of the queued operation. Pass it to [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

status.description: The cluster's status after the request was accepted, `provisioning` for a create or `deleting` for a delete. On a replay it is the cluster's current status (`deleted` once it is gone). This is not the operation's status; use `is_completed` or [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) for that.

events_url.description: Path of the server-sent events stream with the operation's progress.

is_replay.description: `true` when an existing operation was returned for a reused `X-Idempotency` key.

is_completed.description: `true` when a replayed operation has already finished. Omitted unless `true`.

cpu_limit_millis.description: Maximum CPU in millicores the app can burst to.

included_egress_gib.description: Included outbound transfer per month in GiB.

hourly_price_cents.description: Hourly price in whole cents. Often `0` for cheap plans; use `hourly_price_micros`.

hourly_price_micros.description: Hourly price in millionths of the currency unit.

remaining.description: Free plan apps that can still be created.

building.description: Deployments whose display status is building, updating, queued or deploying.

status.description:
Lifecycle state. `provisioning` while being created, resized, restored or restarted,
`ready` when usable, `deleting` while being deleted and `failed` when the last create,
resize, restore, restart or delete failed. `deleted` only appears in an idempotent replay
of a delete.

`stopped` means the platform stopped the database because the account was suspended
for non-payment. A `ready` database switches to `stopped` as soon as the stop is queued
(compute billing stops), and stays stopped while the account is suspended. Within about
a minute of the account becoming active again it is restarted: it goes through
`provisioning` back to `ready` (or `failed` if the restart fails). While `stopped`,
actions that need a `ready` database (resize, password rotation, snapshots, the data
browser) return `409`. If the stop itself fails, the database stays `ready` and the stop
is retried.

tags.name: Account
tags.description:
Your own account: your profile and billing details, the acceptable use policy you must accept
before creating resources, and your activity log.

These endpoints belong to you, not to a workspace, so they do not take an `X-Workspace-Slug`
header.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description:
Workspaces group resources and the people who can manage them. Every VM, snapshot and SSH key
lives in a workspace, and most endpoints act on the workspace named in the `X-Workspace-Slug`
header.

**Roles.** Each member has one role:

| Role | Can |
|---|---|
| `owner` | Everything, including billing and deleting the workspace. Each workspace has exactly one owner, the person who created it. |
| `admin` | Manage resources, settings, members and invitations, read the audit log, and delete SSH keys other members added to the workspace. Cannot invite or promote other admins, or change or remove another admin. |
| `developer` | Create, change and delete resources, connect to them, and manage secrets and their own SSH keys. |
| `viewer` | Read-only access to the workspace's resources. |

**Workspace UID and slug.** Routes under `/v1/workspaces/{workspace_uid}/...` (notifications,
settings, members and invitations) need both the workspace's `uid` in the path and its slug in
`X-Workspace-Slug`. They must name the same workspace, otherwise the request fails with `403`
(`workspace not found or access denied`). Listing, creating and deleting workspaces, and the
`/v1/workspace-invitations/{token}` routes, do not use the header.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description:
Personal API keys authenticate the CLI, the Rumpty MCP and your own automation. Keys belong to
you, not to a workspace, and inherit your role in each workspace you access.

tags.name: SSH Keys
tags.description:
SSH public keys you can install on VMs. Pass their `uid`s as `ssh_key_uids` when you
[create a VM](/api/virtual-machines/create-a-vm).

A key belongs both to you and to the workspace you add it in. In a workspace you can use
your own keys (including ones you added in other workspaces) and every key other members added
to that workspace. Only the public key is stored. It is never returned by the API, only its
fingerprint.

tags.name: Virtual Machines
tags.description:
Create and manage virtual machines (VMs) in a workspace: pick a plan, image and zone, control
the VM's power state, resize it, read its metrics, expose ports over HTTPS, attach custom
domains and run one-off commands.

Most write actions are asynchronous. They queue an operation and return `202 Accepted` with an
`operation_id`. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) to follow it.

tags.name: Snapshots
tags.description:
Point-in-time copies of a VM's disk. Take snapshots from a VM, restore a VM to one, or create
a new VM from one. Snapshots belong to the workspace and survive deletion of their source VM.
Creating, restoring and deleting snapshots are asynchronous operations.

tags.name: Operations
tags.description:
Every asynchronous action (creating a VM, starting it, taking a snapshot, exposing an app and
so on) is recorded as an operation. Operations move through `queued`, `running` and finally
`succeeded` or `failed`.

tags.name: Kubernetes
tags.description:
Managed Kubernetes clusters built on [k3s](https://k3s.io). A cluster is one control-plane node
and one to three worker nodes, each running on its own compute plan. When the cluster is ready
you get a public API `endpoint` and a `kubeconfig` to use with `kubectl`.

Creating and deleting clusters is asynchronous. Both return `202 Accepted` with an
`operation_id`. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) or
[Get a cluster](/api/kubernetes/get-a-cluster) to follow progress. Send `X-Idempotency` to
make retries safe: a repeated request returns the original operation with `200 OK`.

If the account is suspended for non-payment, running clusters are powered off (`stopped`)
and restarted automatically once the account is active again.

tags.name: Deployments
tags.description:
Deployments build and run your application from a Git repository. Point a deployment at a
repository and branch, pick a plan, and RumptyCloud builds a container image (with Railpack or
your Dockerfile), runs it, and serves it over HTTPS on a `rumptycloud.app` hostname. You can
add custom domains, environment variables, a persistent volume, scale-to-zero and
autoscaling.

Every build or rollout is a **run**. Runs keep their build logs and, while the image is
retained, can be redeployed later to roll back.

Builds, rollouts, restarts, plan changes and deletion are asynchronous. They return
`202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation)
to follow one.

Send an optional `X-Idempotency` header to make retries safe. The key is looked up before
anything else is checked, so a retry gets the original result even if the first request
already changed the deployment (for example, deleted it). If the key was already used for
the same action, the original operation is returned with `200 OK`, `is_replay: true` and
an `X-Idempotency-Replay: true` header, and nothing new is queued. If the original
operation has finished, `is_completed` is `true` and `X-Idempotency-Completed: true` is
set. Reusing a key for a different action or a different deployment returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are scoped to the workspace owner's account and
the workspace. Requests that queue no operation (create without `deploy_now`, a plan
change with nothing live) do not record the key, so repeating one runs it again.

If the account is suspended for non-payment, live apps are paused (`status: paused`) and
builds, rollouts, restarts, environment applies and plan changes are rejected with `402`
and `action: past_due` (as they are while the account is past due). Git pushes no longer
trigger auto-deploys and pull requests no longer get previews. Once the
account is active again, apps that suspension paused are resumed automatically within
about a minute.

tags.name: Apps
tags.description:
One-click apps install ready-made software, such as WordPress or Uptime Kuma, from a catalog
of templates. An app is a group of managed [deployments](/api/deployments/list-deployments)
called **components**: usually a public `web` component plus private backing services such as
a `database`, each with its own plan and persistent volume. Components run pinned, prebuilt
images instead of building from a Git repository, and their passwords and secrets are
generated for you.

A regular deployment is something you build from your own code and manage directly. An app
owns its components: they are created and deleted together, they carry an `app_uid`, they are
left out of [List deployments](/api/deployments/list-deployments), and they cannot be deleted
or moved to another plan on their own. You can still read and manage a component through the
deployment endpoints, for example to add a custom domain to the web component or read its
metrics.

tags.name: Git Connections
tags.description:
Connect GitHub accounts and organizations to a workspace through the RumptyCloud GitHub App,
so deployments can build from your repositories. Once connected, list the repositories and
branches the app can see and detect how a repository should be built.

A workspace can have several GitHub connections, one per GitHub account or organization.
Connecting a new account happens in the browser on GitHub: get an install URL with
[Get the GitHub App install URL](/api/git-connections/get-the-github-app-install-url) and open
it. If you already connected the account in another workspace, you can
[link that connection](/api/git-connections/link-a-github-app-installation) instead.

tags.name: Databases
tags.description:
Managed PostgreSQL, MySQL and Redis-compatible (Valkey) databases. Pick a plan and engine
version, read the connection details and credentials, browse data with read-only queries,
take snapshots, resize to another plan and follow metrics.

Creating, resizing, deleting, rotating the password and every snapshot action are
asynchronous. They queue an operation and return its `operation_id`. Poll
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) to follow it.

Databases are owned by the workspace owner's account. Every database endpoint only sees
databases created in the workspace named by `X-Workspace-Slug`.

tags.name: Volumes
tags.description:
Block storage volumes you can attach to a VM for extra disk space. A volume lives on its own,
so its data survives detaching it or deleting the VM it was attached to. A volume can be
attached to one VM at a time, and the VM must be in the same zone.

Creating, attaching, detaching and deleting volumes are asynchronous. They return
`202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation)
or [Get a volume](/api/volumes/get-a-volume) to follow progress. Send `X-Idempotency` to
make retries safe: a repeated request returns the original operation with `200 OK`.

tags.name: Buckets
tags.description:
S3-compatible object storage buckets for files such as images, documents and video. A bucket
is either `public` (objects are served from a public URL) or `private` (objects are read
through short-lived signed URLs).

Creating and deleting a bucket is asynchronous. The request returns `202 Accepted` with an
`operation_id`. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) to follow it.

To upload a file, use three steps:

1. [Create an upload](/api/buckets/create-an-upload) to get a presigned `upload_url`.
2. `PUT` the file's bytes to that URL with the returned headers.
3. [Complete an upload](/api/buckets/complete-an-upload) to mark the object ready.

For direct S3 access from your own tools, create a
[bucket access key](/api/buckets/create-a-bucket-access-key).

The first 10 GiB of file storage per account is free. Uploads that would go over the free
allowance are rejected while billing for storage is not enabled.

tags.name: Firewall Policies
tags.description:
Firewall policies control which traffic can reach your VMs, databases and deployments. A
policy is a named set of allow rules (protocol, port range and source CIDR). Attach a policy
to a resource to enforce it. Policies belong to the workspace and can be attached to many
resources.

A resource with no policy attached is not filtered. Once one or more policies are attached,
only inbound traffic matching an allow rule of one of them is let through. Rules are
allow-only: there are no deny rules.

Changing rules or attachments queues a `firewall.apply` operation for every affected
resource. Where a response includes an `operation_id`, you can follow it with
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

tags.name: Billing
tags.description:
Your prepaid wallet, saved cards, current usage and invoices.

Billing belongs to your account, not to a workspace, so these endpoints take no
`X-Workspace-Slug` header. Resources are billed to the owner of the workspace they run in, so
your usage and invoices cover the workspaces you own.

Amounts are kept in US dollars. Fields ending in `_cents` are US cents and fields ending in
`_micros` are millionths of a dollar (10,000 micros = 1 cent). Customers billed in Nigeria see
and pay amounts in naira: `display_currency` and `exchange_rate` tell you how to convert, and
fields ending in `_minor` are in the minor unit of that currency (kobo for NGN).

Every billing endpoint, including the wallet and saved card endpoints, needs a verified email
address and returns `403` with `action: verify_email` otherwise.

If usage goes unpaid, your account becomes `past_due` and then `suspended` (see
`billing_status` in [Get your profile](/api/account/get-your-profile)). Suspension powers
off your VMs, databases, Kubernetes clusters and deployments. Paying what you owe makes the
account `active` again, and everything suspension powered off is started again
automatically within about a minute.

get.description:
Returns the account the API key belongs to, including the workspaces you are an active member
of and your role and permissions in each.

`billing_country` is the country used for tax: the value you set with
[Update your profile](/api/account/update-your-profile), or the country detected when you
signed up if you never set one.

patch.description:
Updates your billing details. Only the fields you send are changed. Send an empty string to
clear a field.

Your billing country decides the tax applied to your invoices and the currency amounts are
displayed and charged in. A tax ID marks you as a business customer and is printed on your
invoices.

Returns your full profile, the same shape as [Get your profile](/api/account/get-your-profile).

billing_country.description: Your tax residence as a 2-letter ISO 3166-1 country code. Trimmed and upper-cased. Send `""` to clear it, in which case the country detected at signup is used again.

tax_id.description: Your VAT number or tax identification number. Trimmed. Send `""` to clear it.

200.description: The profile was updated. Returns your full profile.

400.description: Validation failed: `invalid request` (malformed JSON or a field is not a string), `billing_country must be a 2-letter ISO country code`, or `tax_id is too long`.

example.message: billing_country must be a 2-letter ISO country code

get.description:
Reports whether you have accepted the current versions of the policies that make up the
acceptable use policy: the privacy and data policy (`privacy_data_policy`) and the fair use
policy (`fair_use_policy`).

`accepted` is `true` only when every policy is accepted at its current version. Until then,
creating a VM, a deployment or an app returns `428 Precondition Required` with
`action: accept_acceptable_use_policy`. Accept with
[Accept the acceptable use policy](/api/account/accept-the-acceptable-use-policy).

post.description:
Accepts the current version of every policy in the acceptable use policy for your account.
You must do this once before you can [create a VM](/api/virtual-machines/create-a-vm),
a deployment or an app. Those endpoints return `428` until you have.

No request body is needed. The acceptance is recorded with the time, your IP address and your
user agent. Calling it again is safe: it refreshes `accepted_at`.

Returns the updated status, the same shape as
[Get acceptable use policy status](/api/account/get-acceptable-use-policy-status).

get.description:
Returns audit log entries, newest first. Only actions that change something (creating,
updating, deleting, starting a VM and so on) are recorded. Reads are not logged. Each action
is logged whether it succeeded or failed.

There are two views:

- **Your activity** (default): every entry where you were the actor, across all workspaces.
- **Workspace trail**: send the `workspace_slug` query parameter to get every member's
  entries for that workspace. You need the owner or admin role in the workspace.

This endpoint does **not** read the `X-Workspace-Slug` header. Use the `workspace_slug` query
parameter to select a workspace.

Paging details are in a top-level `meta` object next to `data`. Entry fields use PascalCase
names. Entries identify the acting user and the workspace by UID only (`UserUID`,
`WorkspaceUID`); they do not include account or workspace details.

parameters.name: workspace_slug
parameters.description: Slug of a workspace to return the shared audit trail for. Requires the owner or admin role in that workspace. Omit it to get your own activity.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
Filter by action. A value ending in `.success` or `.failed` matches exactly. Any other
value matches every outcome of that action, so `vm.create` matches `vm.create.success`
and `vm.create.failed`.

parameters.name: resource_type
parameters.description: Only return entries for this resource type, e.g. `vm`, `snapshot`, `ssh_key`, `workspace_member`.

parameters.name: resource_uid
parameters.description: Only return entries about the resource with this UID.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only return entries created at or after this time (RFC 3339). An invalid value is ignored.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only return entries created at or before this time (RFC 3339). An invalid value is ignored.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Values below 1 return the first page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Entries per page. Defaults to `50`. Values below 1 or above `200` fall back to `50`.

data.description: The entries on this page, newest first.

page.description: The page that was returned. Values below 1 (or non-numbers) are reported as `1`.

page_size.description: The page size that was used. Values below 1 or above `200` (or non-numbers) are reported as `50`.

403.description: The workspace in `workspace_slug` does not exist or you are not a member (`workspace not found or access denied`), or your role cannot read its audit log (`you do not have permission to view this workspace's audit log`).

example.message: you do not have permission to view this workspace's audit log

get.description:
Returns every workspace you are an active member of, newest first, with your role and
permissions in each. This endpoint needs no `X-Workspace-Slug` header.

Without query parameters, every workspace is returned in `data`. Send `page` or `page_size` to
paginate. A top-level `pagination` object is then added next to `data`, and `q` filters the
results. `q` is ignored unless `page` or `page_size` is present.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Values below 1 (or non-numbers) are treated as `1`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `10`. Values above `100` are capped at `100`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring search across the workspace's name, slug and description. Only applied when paginating.

200.description: Your workspaces. `pagination` is only present when `page` or `page_size` was sent.

post.description:
Creates a workspace and makes you its owner. This endpoint needs no `X-Workspace-Slug` header.

The slug is generated from the name plus the first 8 characters of the new workspace's `uid`,
so `Staging` becomes something like `staging-019a8f2c`. Use the returned `slug` in
`X-Workspace-Slug` for requests in the new workspace. Workspace names do not have to be
unique.

name.description: Display name. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Must contain at least one letter or digit.

201.description: The workspace was created. You are its owner.

400.description: Validation failed: `invalid request` (malformed JSON or `name` missing), `workspace name cannot be empty`, or `workspace name must contain alphanumeric characters`.

example.message: workspace name must contain alphanumeric characters

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a workspace you own, together with its members, pending invitations and
any leftover records. The audit history is kept but no longer linked to the workspace. This
endpoint needs no `X-Workspace-Slug` header.

You can only delete a workspace when:

- you are its owner (other members get `404`),
- it is not your default workspace, and
- it has no VMs, volumes, databases, Kubernetes clusters, storage buckets or deployments left.
  Delete those first.

The response contains the deleted workspace. `role` and `permissions` are not included.

403.description: The workspace cannot be deleted: `default workspace cannot be deleted` or `workspace still has resources; delete the resources first`.

example.message: workspace still has resources; delete the resources first

404.description: No workspace with this `uid` is owned by you (`workspace not found`).

get.description:
Reports whether the workspace has an alert webhook. The webhook URL itself is stored encrypted
and never returned.

Requires the owner or admin role.

patch.description:
Sets or removes the workspace's alert webhook. When set, workspace alerts (for example an app
that keeps crashing) are also sent as an HTTP `POST` to this URL, in addition to email. You
can use a Discord webhook URL or any HTTPS endpoint.

- Send a URL to set or replace the webhook.
- Send `""` to remove it.
- Omit `webhook_url` (or send `null`) to leave it unchanged.

Requires the owner or admin role.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS URL to post alerts to. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Must use `https` and include a host. Send `""` to remove the webhook.

400.description: Validation failed: `invalid request` (malformed JSON), `webhook URL must be 2048 characters or less`, `webhook URL is not valid`, or `webhook URL must use https`.

get.description:
Returns the workspace's settings.

Requires the owner or admin role.

patch.description:
Changes the workspace's settings. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

`vm_exec_enabled` controls whether [Run a command on a VM](/api/virtual-machines/run-a-command-on-a-vm)
is allowed in this workspace. It is off by default. AI assistants use that endpoint to run
commands on your VMs.

Requires the owner or admin role.

vm_exec_enabled.description: Allow running commands on the workspace's VMs through the API.

200.description: The settings were saved. Returns the current settings.

get.description:
Returns the workspace's members in the order they joined, with each member's role and
permissions. `is_current_user` marks you.

Any workspace role can call this.

patch.description:
Changes a member's role to `admin`, `developer` or `viewer`. The new permissions apply to the
member's next request.

Requires the owner or admin role. Some changes are not allowed:

- The owner's role cannot be changed, and no one can be made owner.
- Admins cannot give anyone the `admin` role, and cannot change another admin's role.

200.description: The role was changed. Returns the updated member. `invited_by` is not included in this response.

400.description: Validation failed: `role is required` (missing or malformed body) or `role must be admin, developer, or viewer`.

example.message: role must be admin, developer, or viewer

403.description:
Not allowed: your role cannot manage members, `the workspace owner role cannot be changed`,
`admins cannot assign the admin role`, or `admins cannot change another admin's role`.

example.message: the workspace owner role cannot be changed

404.description: No member with this `uid` in the workspace (`workspace member not found`).

delete.description:
Removes a member from the workspace. They lose access immediately. Resources they created stay
in the workspace.

Requires the owner or admin role. You cannot remove yourself or the owner, and admins cannot
remove another admin.

The response contains the member as they were before removal.

403.description:
Not allowed: your role cannot manage members, `you cannot remove yourself from the workspace`,
`the workspace owner cannot be removed`, or `admins cannot remove another admin`.

example.message: the workspace owner cannot be removed

404.description: No member with this `uid` in the workspace (`workspace member not found`).

get.description:
Returns the workspace's pending invitations, newest first. Accepted, revoked and expired
invitations are not listed.

Requires the owner or admin role.

post.description:
Emails an invitation to join the workspace. The email contains a link with a secret token. The
token is never returned by the API. The invitee opens the link, signs in or signs up with the
invited email address, and accepts. See
[Accept an invitation](/api/workspaces/accept-an-invitation).

Invitations expire after 72 hours. Use
[Resend an invitation](/api/workspaces/resend-an-invitation) to send a fresh link.

Requires the owner or admin role. Admins cannot invite someone as `admin`.

email.description: Email address to invite. It is trimmed and lower-cased before use.

role.description: Role the invitee gets when they accept.

201.description: The invitation was created and the email queued.

400.description: Validation failed: `email and role are required`, `a valid email address is required`, or `role must be admin, developer, or viewer`.

example.message: a valid email address is required

403.description: Your role cannot manage members, or you are an admin inviting someone as `admin` (`admins cannot assign the admin role`).

example.message: admins cannot assign the admin role

409.description:
Conflict: `you are already a member of this workspace` (you invited yourself),
`user is already a member of this workspace`, or
`a pending invitation already exists for this email`.

example.message: a pending invitation already exists for this email

post.description:
Emails a pending invitation again with a new link. The previous link stops working, and the
invitation's expiry is reset to 72 hours from now. No request body is needed.

Requires the owner or admin role.

404.description: No invitation with this `uid` in the workspace (`invitation not found`).

409.description: The invitation was already accepted, revoked or marked expired (`invitation is no longer pending`).

delete.description:
Revokes a pending invitation. Its link stops working straight away.

Requires the owner or admin role.

200.description: The invitation was revoked. Returns it with `status` set to `revoked`.

404.description: No invitation with this `uid` in the workspace (`invitation not found`).

409.description: The invitation was already accepted, revoked or marked expired (`invitation is no longer pending`).

get.description:
Returns the basic details of an invitation from the token in its email link, so a signed-out
invitee can be sent to sign in or sign up. `account_exists` tells you which.

This endpoint is public and needs no API key or workspace: holding the token is the
credential. `status` is reported as `expired` once the invitation is past its expiry, even if
it was never marked expired. Responses are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

404.description: The token does not match any invitation (`invitation not found`).

get.description:
Returns an invitation addressed to you, with the workspace it is for, so you can review it
before [accepting it](/api/workspaces/accept-an-invitation). Use the token from the
invitation email.

Needs a verified account whose email matches the invited address. No `X-Workspace-Slug`
header is needed, since you may not belong to any workspace yet. If the invitation has
expired, it is marked expired and `409` is returned. Responses are sent with
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

403.description: Your email is not verified (`action: verify_email`), or the invitation was sent to a different address (`this invitation was sent to a different email address`).

example.message: this invitation was sent to a different email address

404.description: The token does not match any invitation (`invitation not found`).

409.description: `invitation is no longer pending` (already accepted, revoked or expired) or `invitation has expired`.

post.description:
Accepts an invitation addressed to you and adds you to the workspace with the invited role.
The inviter is emailed that you joined. No request body is needed.

Needs a verified account whose email matches the invited address. No `X-Workspace-Slug`
header is needed. Use the returned `slug` in `X-Workspace-Slug` for requests in the
workspace you joined. Responses are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: You joined the workspace. Returns it with your new role and permissions. `member_count` is always `0` in this response.

403.description: Your email is not verified (`action: verify_email`), or the invitation was sent to a different address (`this invitation was sent to a different email address`).

example.message: this invitation was sent to a different email address

404.description: The token does not match any invitation (`invitation not found`).

409.description: `invitation is no longer pending`, `invitation has expired`, or `you are already a member of this workspace`.

example.message: you are already a member of this workspace

post.description:
Creates a personal API key. The full `token` appears **only in this response**. Store it
securely, because it cannot be retrieved again.

Keys expire after 365 days by default. Set `expires_in_days` to choose a lifetime (capped at
730 days), or set `never_expires` to `true`. Do not send both.

name.description: Label for the key. Must be unique among your keys.

expires_in_days.description: Days until the key expires. Defaults to `365`. Values above `730` are capped at `730`.

never_expires.description: Create a key that never expires. Cannot be combined with `expires_in_days`.

scope.description: What the key is for. `cli` covers the CLI and REST API. `mcp` is for the Rumpty MCP server.

201.description: The key was created. The response includes the one-time `token`.

token.description: The full secret token. Shown only once.

example.message: API key created. Copy the token now. It will not be shown again.

400.description: Validation failed: `name` is missing or already used, `scope` is not `cli` or `mcp`, or both `never_expires` and `expires_in_days` were sent.

example.message: an API key with this name already exists.

get.description: Returns your active API keys. Secret tokens are never returned, only the `prefix` that identifies each key.

delete.description: Revokes the key immediately. Requests using it are rejected with `401` from then on.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: The key's `uid`.

post.description:
Adds an SSH public key to your account and to the workspace. The key must be a single line in
OpenSSH `authorized_keys` format, such as the contents of `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`.

Names and keys are unique per account, across all your workspaces: you cannot add two keys
with the same name, or the same key twice.

Requires the owner, admin or developer role. Viewers get `403`.

name.description: Label for the key. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Must be unique among your keys.

public_key.description: The public key in OpenSSH `authorized_keys` format (`<type> <base64> [comment]`). Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.

400.description:
Validation failed: `invalid request` (malformed JSON, or `name` or `public_key` missing or
empty), `name and public_key are required` (a field is only whitespace),
`invalid ssh public key`, `an ssh key with this name already exists`, or
`this ssh key has already been added to your account`. A missing `X-Workspace-Slug`
header returns `workspace is required`.

example.message: an ssh key with this name already exists

get.description:
Returns the SSH keys you can use in this workspace, newest first: every key you added (in any
workspace) plus every key other members added to this workspace. Deleted keys are not listed.

Any workspace role can call this.

200.description: The SSH keys usable in this workspace.

delete.description:
Deletes an SSH key.

- Your own keys can be deleted from any workspace you have the developer role or higher in,
  including keys you added in another workspace.
- A key another member added can only be deleted by an owner or admin of the workspace it
  was added in, and only through that workspace. Otherwise the call returns `403`
  (`you can only delete your own ssh keys`).

Deleting a key only removes it from RumptyCloud, so it can no longer be chosen for new VMs.
This endpoint does not change VMs that already have the key installed.

Requires the owner, admin or developer role. Viewers get `403`.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: The key's `uid`.

403.description: Your role cannot delete keys, or the key belongs to another member and you are not an owner or admin of this workspace.

example.message: you can only delete your own ssh keys

404.description: No key with this `uid` is usable in this workspace (`ssh key not found`): it is neither yours nor added to this workspace.

get.description:
Returns the compute plans you can create a VM on, cheapest first. Only plans that are
currently available are listed.

This endpoint is public and needs no API key or workspace.

Returns the enabled operating system images you can create a VM from, grouped by family.
Database engine images are not included.

This endpoint is public and needs no API key or workspace.

Returns the zones VMs can run in. There is currently one zone, `olas-closet`, which is also
the default when you create a VM without a `zone_slug`.

This endpoint is public and needs no API key or workspace.

Returns the workspace's VMs, newest first. Deleted VMs are not included.

Without query parameters, every VM is returned in `data`. Send `page` or `page_size` to
paginate. A top-level `pagination` object is then added next to `data`, and `q` filters the
results. `q` is ignored unless `page` or `page_size` is present.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Values below 1 (or non-numbers) are treated as `1`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `10`. Values above `100` are capped at `100`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring search across the VM's name, slug, private IP, app hostname, status and display status. Only applied when paginating.

200.description: The workspace's VMs. `pagination` is only present when `page` or `page_size` was sent.

post.description:
Queues a new VM and returns `202 Accepted` with the `operation_id` of the create operation.
The VM starts in `provisioning`. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation)
or [Get a VM](/api/virtual-machines/get-a-vm) to see when it is `running`.

`X-Idempotency` is optional but recommended. If you repeat a request with the same key and
the same `name`, you get the original operation back with `200 OK` and
`X-Idempotency-Replay: true`, and nothing new is queued. The replay check runs after the
basic field checks (required fields, SSH keys, zone) but before the billing, plan, image,
quota and name checks, so a retry after the VM was created still returns the original
operation.
Reusing the key with a different `name` returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.
Without a key, every request queues a new VM.

Things to know:

- You must accept the acceptable use policy before creating your first VM. Until then this
  endpoint returns `428` with `action: accept_acceptable_use_policy`.
- Provide `image_slug`, or `snapshot_uid` to create the VM from a snapshot. A VM created from
  a snapshot uses the snapshot's image and login user and is always persistent.
- New VMs from an image log in as `root`.
- If the plan is ephemeral-eligible, the VM is ephemeral even when `ephemeral` is `false`.
  Ephemeral VMs expire after the plan's `default_runtime_mins` (72 hours if the plan sets
  none). Each account can have one active ephemeral VM.
- Desktop images need a plan with at least 2 vCPU and 2048 MiB of memory.
- The VM gets an HTTPS app URL that forwards to port `8080` by default. Change it with
  [Set the VM app port](/api/virtual-machines/set-the-vm-app-port).
- VM names must be unique in the workspace. Uniqueness is checked on the slug of the name,
  so `Web 1` and `web-1` clash.

name.description: Display name of the VM. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Its slug must be unique among the workspace's VMs.

plan_slug.description: Slug of a compute plan from [List plans](/api/virtual-machines/list-plans). Case-insensitive.

image_slug.description: Slug of an image from [List images](/api/virtual-machines/list-images). Required unless `snapshot_uid` is set, and ignored when it is.

vpc_slug.description: Slug of the VPC to attach the VM to. Use `default` for the platform's default private network.

zone_slug.description: Zone to run the VM in. Defaults to `olas-closet`, currently the only zone.

ssh_key_uids.description: UIDs of SSH keys to install on the VM. At least one is required. Each key must be yours or belong to the workspace.

ephemeral.description: Request a short-lived ephemeral VM. Only allowed on ephemeral-eligible plans. On those plans the VM is ephemeral whatever you send. Ignored when `snapshot_uid` is set.

snapshot_uid.description: UID of an `available` snapshot in this workspace to create the VM from. When set, `image_slug` is not needed.

startup_script.description: Optional shell script to run on the VM's first boot.

200.description: Replay. The `X-Idempotency` key was already used to create a VM with this name, so the existing operation is returned and nothing is queued. `status` is the operation's current status and `vm_status` the VM's current status (`deleted` once the VM is gone).

X-Idempotency-Completed.description: `true` when the original operation has already finished.

example.message: existing operation still in progress; not queued again

400.description:
Validation failed. Possible messages: `invalid request` (malformed JSON),
`name, plan_slug, and vpc_slug are required`, `image_slug is required`,
`at least one ssh key is required`, `invalid zone`, `invalid compute plan`,
`this compute plan is not available`, `invalid image`, `invalid snapshot`,
`snapshot source image is unavailable`,
`selected plan is not eligible for ephemeral compute`, `invalid ssh key`, `invalid vpc`,
or the desktop plan-size message.

example.message: at least one ssh key is required

402.description: The account is past due and cannot create new paid resources.

example.message: Your account is past due. Add funds to your wallet to create new paid resources.

409.description:
Conflict: `A VM with this name already exists.`, `ephemeral compute limit reached`,
`snapshot is not ready to restore`, or the `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a
different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: A VM with this name already exists.

428.description: You have not accepted the acceptable use policy yet.

example.message: acceptable use policy acceptance is required before creating a virtual machine

get.description:
Returns VM counts for the workspace. VMs that are deleting or deleted are not counted.
`stopped_vms` is every counted VM that is not `running`, so it includes VMs that are
provisioning or failed.
Returns one VM, including its plan, image, app URL, SSH keys and the latest root disk usage reported by the guest agent.

delete.description:
Queues deletion of the VM. The VM moves to `deleting` straight away and disappears from
listings once the operation finishes. Snapshots of the VM are kept. Find them with
[List snapshots](/api/snapshots/list-snapshots).

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200`, even
after the VM has been deleted.

409.description: The VM is already deleting or deleted (`vm is not available for this action`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: vm is not available for this action

post.description:
Queues a start of a stopped VM. The VM shows `provisioning` until it is running again.

Accounts that are past due, suspended or terminated cannot start VMs and get `402`. VMs
that were stopped because the account was suspended for non-payment are started again
automatically once the account is back in good standing.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200`, even
if the VM is already running by then. The replay is checked before billing, so a retry
still gets the original operation after the account became past due.

402.description: The account is past due, suspended or terminated.

example.message: Your account is past due. Add funds to your wallet to create new paid resources.

409.description: The VM is already running (`vm is already running`), is deleting or deleted (`vm is not available for this action`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

post.description:
Queues a stop. The VM's status changes to `stopped` as soon as the request is accepted.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200`, even
though the VM is already `stopped`. Without a key, a second stop returns `409`
(`vm is already stopped`).

409.description: The VM is already stopped (`vm is already stopped`), is deleting or deleted (`vm is not available for this action`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

post.description:
Queues a reboot. The VM shows `provisioning` until it is running again.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200`.

409.description: The VM is deleting or deleted (`vm is not available for this action`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: vm is not available for this action

post.description:
Moves the VM to a different compute plan. Billing switches to the new plan's rate right
away (usage so far is settled at the old rate first).

- A **running** VM is restarted so the new CPU and memory take effect. It shows
  `provisioning` until it is back.
- A **stopped** VM gets the new resources on its next start.
- The root disk can only grow. Moving to a plan with a larger included disk expands it.
  Plans whose included disk is smaller than the VM's current disk are rejected.
- Ephemeral VMs can only move between ephemeral-eligible plans, and persistent VMs between
  persistent plans.
- VMs on a desktop image need a plan with at least 2 vCPU and 2048 MiB of memory.

The VM must be `running` or `stopped`. This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with
an `operation_id`. See [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an
`X-Idempotency` key to make retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original
operation with `200`, even after the resize has finished. The request body is not
compared on a replay.

plan_slug.description: Slug of the available compute plan to move to. Case-insensitive. Must differ from the current plan.

400.description:
Validation failed: `invalid request`, `plan_slug is required`, `invalid compute plan`,
`this compute plan is not available`, `this plan is not available for this VM type`,
`This VM is already on the <plan> plan.`, the disk-size message, or the desktop
plan-size message.

example.message: This VM is already on the Small plan.

409.description: The VM is not `running` or `stopped` (`vm is not available for this action`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: vm is not available for this action

get.description:
Returns the latest CPU, memory, disk and network sample reported by the guest agent.

If no sample has arrived yet, `available` is `false`, the metric fields are left out and
`unavailable_reason` explains why. `stale` is `true` when the latest sample is more than two
minutes old.

Returns a time series of the VM's metrics over a time range. The step between points
depends on the range:

| `range` | `step_seconds` |
| ------- | -------------- |
| `15m`   | 15             |
| `1h`    | 60             |
| `6h`    | 300            |
| `24h`   | 900            |
| `7d`    | 3600           |
| `30d`   | 21600          |

If no samples exist in the range, `available` is `false` and `points` is empty.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Time window to return, ending now. Case-insensitive.

400.description: `range` is not one of the allowed values (`invalid metrics range`).

get.description:
Returns the firewall policies attached to the VM, with their rules and every resource each
policy is attached to. Returns an empty list when no policy is attached. To attach or detach a
policy, use [Attach a firewall policy](/api/firewall-policies/attach-a-firewall-policy).
Returns the custom domains attached to the VM, with their verification status.

post.description:
Registers a custom domain for the VM's app URL. The domain starts as `pending`. Nothing is
routed until you verify it.

To verify, create two DNS records at your DNS provider, then call
[Verify a custom domain](/api/virtual-machines/verify-a-custom-domain):

- A `CNAME` record for the domain pointing to the VM's `app_hostname`.
- A `TXT` record at `rumpty-challenge.<domain_name>` whose value is the returned
  `verification_txt`.

Root (apex) domains such as `acme.com` are not supported yet. Use a subdomain such as
`www.acme.com`. A domain can only be registered once across RumptyCloud.

domain_name.description: Fully qualified subdomain to attach. Lowercased and trimmed. Must contain only letters, digits, hyphens and dots, and end in a TLD of at least two letters.

201.description: The domain was added in `pending` state.

400.description: Validation failed: `invalid request`, `domain name is required`, `invalid domain name format`, or the domain is a root domain.

example.message: root domains are not supported yet; use a subdomain such as www.acme.com

409.description: The domain is already registered.

delete.description:
Removes the custom domain. It disappears from
[List custom domains](/api/virtual-machines/list-custom-domains) immediately. Its route
is torn down by an `unexpose` operation.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200`, even
though the domain is already gone. Without a key, a retry returns `404`
(`custom domain not found`).

The key is tied to the domain: reusing it for another domain returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`.

202.description: The domain was removed and the route teardown was queued.

post.description:
Checks the domain's DNS records against its authoritative nameserver and, if they match,
queues an `expose` operation that issues a TLS certificate and routes the domain to the
VM's app port. The domain stays `pending` until that operation finishes and becomes
`active`.

The `CNAME` must point to the VM's `app_hostname`, and the `TXT` record at
`rumpty-challenge.<domain_name>` must equal `verification_txt`. If either check fails,
the domain is marked `failed` with the reason in `last_error`, and the request returns
`400` with the same message.

Calling this again is safe:

- If you resend an `X-Idempotency` key already used to verify a domain on this VM, that
  operation is returned with `200` and `X-Idempotency-Replay: true`. Reusing the key for
  another domain returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.
- If the domain is already `active`, you get `202` with `status: succeeded`, an empty
  `operation_id` and `is_replay: false`, and nothing is queued.
- If a verification queued in the last 15 minutes is still running, that operation is
  returned with `202` and `is_replay: false` instead of a new one.

Otherwise this is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

202.description: DNS checks passed and the expose operation was queued, or an existing result was returned.

example.message: custom domain verification and exposure queued

400.description:
DNS verification failed or the domain is a root domain. Example DNS messages: `CNAME record has not propagated or does not point to
<app_hostname>`, `verification TXT record not found or does not match: <verification_txt>`,
`unable to locate authoritative DNS nameservers for domain`.

example.message: CNAME record has not propagated or does not point to brave-otter-6b8d90.rumptycloud.app

get.description: Returns the extra ports exposed on the VM over HTTPS, each with its own public URL.

post.description:
Publishes a port on the VM at its own HTTPS URL, `https://<port>-<vm-host-label>.<domain>`.
The app starts as `pending` and becomes `ready` once the route is live.

Each VM can expose a given port once, and app names (after slugging) must be unique per VM.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation and its app with
`200`, instead of `409` for the name or port that the first request already took.

The key is tied to the VM and the app name (or `port-<port>` when no name is given).
Reusing it on another VM or for another name returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`.

port.description: Port on the VM that the app listens on.

name.description: Name for the exposure. It is converted to a slug (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), which must be 40 characters or fewer. Defaults to `port-<port>`.

protocol.description: Backend protocol. Use `grpc` for gRPC (HTTP/2) services.

200.description: Replay. The `X-Idempotency` key was already used to expose an app, so that operation is returned and nothing is queued. `app` is the app's current state. If the app has since been removed, `app` holds only its `uid`, `vm_uid` and `name`.

X-Idempotency-Completed.description: `true` when the original operation has already finished.

example.message: existing operation already finished; not queued again

400.description: Validation failed: `invalid request` (missing or zero `port`), `port must be between 1 and 65535`, `protocol must be http or grpc`, `name is invalid`, or `name must be 40 characters or fewer`.

example.message: protocol must be http or grpc

409.description:
Conflict: `app exposure name already exists for this vm`,
`app exposure port already exists for this vm`, `vm is not available for app exposure`
(VM deleting or deleted), `http access is not configured`, or the `X-Idempotency` key
was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: app exposure port already exists for this vm

delete.description:
Removes an exposed port's public URL. The app moves to `deleting` and is removed when the
operation finishes. Only apps in `ready` or `failed` state can be removed. If the app is
already `deleting`, its in-flight operation is returned with `200` and `is_replay: true`.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200`, even
after the app has been removed. The key is tied to the VM and the app: reusing it for
another app or VM returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: The app's `slug` (its name is also accepted and converted to a slug).

200.description: Replay. The `X-Idempotency` key was already used to unexpose this app, or the app is already being removed, so the existing operation is returned and nothing is queued. If the app is already gone, `app` holds only its `uid`, `vm_uid` and `name`.

X-Idempotency-Completed.description: `true` when the original operation has already finished.

409.description:
Conflict: `app exposure is still being provisioned` (app is `pending`),
`app exposure is already being removed`,
`app exposure cannot be removed in its current state`,
`vm is not available for this action`, or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a
different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: app exposure is still being provisioned

put.description:
Points the VM's own app URL (`app_url`) at a different port on the VM. The VM's `app_port`
only changes once the switch has finished, so it always shows the port being served.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200`, even
after the port has switched. The same key with a different `port` returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`.

port.description: Port on the VM that the app URL should forward to. Must differ from the current `app_port`.

400.description: Validation failed: `invalid request` (missing or zero `port`) or `port must be between 1 and 65535`.

409.description:
Conflict: `the app url already serves port <port>`, `this vm has no app url`,
`vm is not available for this action` (VM deleting or deleted), or the `X-Idempotency`
key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: the app url already serves port 3000

post.summary: Run a command on a VM
post.description:
Runs one non-interactive command on a running VM over SSH and waits for it to finish. The
command runs as `bash -lc '<command>'`.

- Command execution through the API is **off by default**. A workspace owner or admin must
  turn it on in workspace settings, otherwise this returns `403`.
- Requires the `runtime connect` permission (owner, admin or developer role).
- The command times out after 30 seconds by default, or `timeout_seconds` (max 60).
- `stdout` and `stderr` are each capped at 64 KiB. Truncation is flagged in the response.
- Each user can have at most 4 console sessions and commands open at once.
- The first command on an older VM may return `409` while command access is set up. Retry
  after about 30 seconds.

A non-zero `exit_code` is still a `200` response. When the command times out, `timed_out`
is `true` and `exit_code` is usually `124`, or `-1` if the VM never returned one.

command.description: Shell command to run. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed. At most 8192 bytes.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to let the command run. Values above `60` are capped at `60`. `0` or omitted means `30`.

200.description: The command ran. Check `exit_code` to see whether it succeeded.

data.stdout:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/vda1        20G  4.0G   16G  20% /

400.description: `command` is missing or empty (`command is required`), or longer than 8192 bytes (`command is too long`).

403.description: Your role cannot connect to VMs, or command execution is turned off for this workspace.

example.message: running commands through the API is turned off for this workspace; a workspace owner or admin can turn it on in workspace settings

409.description:
The command could not be run right now: `vm is not running`,
`vm network route is not ready`,
`too many open console sessions or commands; try again shortly`,
`enabling command access on this VM; retry in about 30 seconds`,
`this VM can't accept commands yet; connect with SSH instead`, or
`unable to reach the VM over SSH`.

get.description: Returns the snapshots taken from this VM, newest first. Use [List snapshots](/api/snapshots/list-snapshots) to include snapshots whose source VM has been deleted.

post.description:
Queues a snapshot of the VM's disk. The snapshot starts as `creating` and becomes
`available` when it is ready. `consumed_bytes` is filled in then.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). The new snapshot's UID is the
operation's `resource_uid`. In the response, `name` is the VM's name, not the snapshot's.

Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make retries safe: a retry with the same key returns the
original operation with `200` and nothing new is queued. The key is tied to the VM and
the snapshot `name`: reusing it for another VM or name returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`.

name.description: Name of the snapshot. Its slug is derived from it.

shutdown_before_snapshot.description: Shut the VM down before taking the snapshot, for a consistent copy of a busy disk.

400.description: `name` is missing or longer than 100 characters (`invalid request payload`).

409.description: The VM is deleting or deleted (`vm is not available for snapshots`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: vm is not available for snapshots

post.description:
Restores the VM from one of its own snapshots. The snapshot must be `available`. While
the restore runs, the snapshot shows `restoring` and the VM shows `provisioning`.

To start a new VM from a snapshot instead, pass `snapshot_uid` to
[Create a VM](/api/virtual-machines/create-a-vm).

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key for the same snapshot returns the original
operation with `200`, even after the restore has finished.

404.description: The VM or snapshot does not exist, or the snapshot was not taken from this VM.

409.description: The snapshot is not `available` (`snapshot is not in available state for restore`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: snapshot is not in available state for restore

delete.description:
Deletes one of the VM's snapshots. The snapshot shows `deleting` until the operation
finishes. To delete a snapshot whose VM no longer exists, use
[Delete a snapshot](/api/snapshots/delete-a-snapshot).

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key for the same snapshot returns the original
operation with `200`, even after the snapshot is gone.

202.description: The delete operation was queued. `name` is the VM's name.

404.description: The VM or snapshot does not exist, or the snapshot was not taken from this VM.

409.description: The snapshot is already being deleted (`snapshot is already being deleted`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

get.description:
Returns every VM snapshot in the workspace, newest first. This includes detached
snapshots (`detached: true`) whose source VM has been deleted.
Returns one snapshot in the workspace, whether or not its source VM still exists.

delete.description:
Deletes a snapshot by UID. Unlike [Delete a VM snapshot](/api/snapshots/delete-a-vm-snapshot),
this works for detached snapshots whose source VM has been deleted. The snapshot shows
`deleting` until the operation finishes.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). Send an `X-Idempotency` key to make
retries safe: a retry with the same key for the same snapshot returns the original
operation with `200`, even after the snapshot is gone. On that replay `vm_uid` is empty.

202.description: The delete operation was queued. Here `name` is the snapshot's name and `vm_uid` is the source VM's UID.

409.description: The snapshot is already being deleted (`snapshot is already being deleted`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

get.description:
Returns all operations in the workspace, newest first. This covers every resource type, not
only VMs, and is not paginated.

Returns one operation. Poll this after any asynchronous action until `status` is
`succeeded` or `failed`. `started_at` and `finished_at` appear once the operation has
started and finished.

parameters.name: operation_id
parameters.description: The operation's `uid`, as returned in `operation_id` by the action that queued it.

get.description:
Returns the workspace's Kubernetes clusters, newest first, with their nodes. Deleted clusters
are not included. This endpoint is not paginated.

The list never includes `kubeconfig` (and does not set `kubeconfig_restricted`). Use
[Get a cluster](/api/kubernetes/get-a-cluster) to read it.

post.description:
Queues a new Kubernetes cluster and returns `202 Accepted` with the `operation_id` of the
create operation. The cluster and its nodes start in `provisioning`. Poll
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) or
[Get a cluster](/api/kubernetes/get-a-cluster) until the cluster is `running`.

Every field except `name` is optional:

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | `v1.36.2+k3s1` |
| `image_slug` | `ubuntu-2404-lts` |
| `control_plane_plan_slug` | `scale` |
| `worker_plan_slug` | `launch` |
| `worker_count` | `1` |

Things to know:

- The cluster runs in the default zone, `olas-closet`.
- Cluster names must be unique in the workspace. Uniqueness is checked on the slug of the
  name, so `Production` and `production` clash.
- Node names are derived from the cluster name: `<name>-cp-1` for the control plane and
  `<name>-worker-1`, `<name>-worker-2` and so on for workers.
- The API `endpoint` has the form
  `https://<slug>-<id>.k8s.rumptycloud.com:16443`, where `<id>` is a short fragment of the
  cluster's `uid`.
- Compute plans must be available. An unavailable plan returns `400`
  (`this compute plan is not available`).
- Past-due and suspended accounts get `402`.
- `X-Idempotency` is optional. A retry with a key you already used for a cluster create
  returns the original operation with `200 OK`, `is_replay: true` and the
  `X-Idempotency-Replay` header, and nothing new is queued. The replay is checked first
  (before billing, validation and the name check), so a retry after the cluster was created
  does not fail with `409` for the name. The same key with a different `name` returns
  `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`. Without a key, a retry of a create that
  already succeeded returns `409` because the name is taken.

name.description: Display name of the cluster. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Its slug must be unique among the workspace's clusters.

version.description: k3s version to install. The API passes it to the provisioner without validating it.

image_slug.description: Slug of the node operating system image. Case-insensitive. Must be an enabled image from [List images](/api/virtual-machines/list-images), except the default `ubuntu-2404-lts`, which can be used even when it is hidden from the VM catalog.

control_plane_plan_slug.description: Compute plan for the control-plane node. Case-insensitive. Must be a compute plan from [List plans](/api/virtual-machines/list-plans).

worker_plan_slug.description: Compute plan for every worker node. Case-insensitive. Must be a compute plan from [List plans](/api/virtual-machines/list-plans).

worker_count.description: Number of worker nodes. `0`, negative values or an omitted field mean `1`. Values above `3` are rejected.

ssh_key_uids.description: UIDs of SSH keys to install on every node. Optional. Each key must be yours or belong to the workspace.

400.description:
Validation failed. Possible messages: `invalid request` (malformed JSON or missing
`name`), `name is required` (blank name), `worker_count cannot exceed 3`,
`invalid compute plan`, `this compute plan is not available`, `invalid image`, or
`invalid ssh key`.

409.description: A cluster with the same name slug already exists in the workspace (`cluster name already exists`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

get.description:
Returns one cluster with its nodes, API `endpoint` and, once available, its `kubeconfig`.

`kubeconfig` contains cluster-admin credentials and is only returned to roles with the
`secrets read` permission (owner, admin or developer). For other roles (viewers) it is
always omitted and `kubeconfig_restricted` is `true`, so an empty kubeconfig does not mean
it is still being generated.
