If the cluster is `running` but its kubeconfig has not arrived yet, this request also asks
the platform to fetch it in the background (at most once every two minutes). Call again
shortly to pick it up.

Deleted clusters are still returned, with status `deleted`.

data.name: production
data.kubeconfig:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
clusters:
  - name: production
    cluster:
      server: https://production-1c2d3e.k8s.rumptycloud.com:16443
      certificate-authority-data: LS0tLS1CRUdJTi...
...

404.description: No cluster with this `uid` exists in the workspace.

delete.description:
Queues deletion of the cluster and all of its nodes. The cluster and its nodes move to
`deleting` straight away, and the cluster disappears from listings once the operation
finishes.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). A cluster can be deleted in any
status except `deleting` and `deleted`, including while it is `stopped`.

`X-Idempotency` is optional. A retry with the same key for the same cluster returns the
original operation with `200 OK` and `is_replay: true`, even after the cluster is gone.
Without a key, a repeated delete returns `409` because the cluster is already deleting.

The response's `cluster` includes `kubeconfig` when one exists.

404.description: No cluster with this `uid` exists in the workspace.

409.description: The cluster is already being deleted or has been deleted (`cluster is already deleting`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

get.description:
Returns the compute plans available for deployments, cheapest first. Only plans that are
currently available are listed. Use a plan's `slug` as `plan_slug` when you
[create a deployment](/api/deployments/create-a-deployment) or
[change its plan](/api/deployments/change-a-deployment-plan).

Plans with `free_allowance_count` above `0` are Free plans. A Free app always scales to zero
when idle, runs a single instance, and counts toward a per-account allowance (see
[Get the free app quota](/api/deployments/get-the-free-app-quota)).

The list can include plans reserved for one-click app components, such as
`deploy-backing`. Those cannot be chosen when creating a deployment or changing a plan
(`invalid deployment plan`).

This endpoint needs an API key but no workspace.

post.description:
Creates a deployment from a Git repository.

- With `deploy_now: true`, the first build is queued straight away. The response is
  `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id` and the new `run`. Follow it with
  [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) or
  [Get a deployment run](/api/deployments/get-a-deployment-run).
- Otherwise the deployment is only saved and the response is `201 Created` without an
  `operation_id`. Start the first build later with
  [Deploy a deployment](/api/deployments/deploy-a-deployment).

Things to know:

- You must accept the acceptable use policy first. Until then this endpoint returns `428`
  with `action: accept_acceptable_use_policy`.
- The deployment gets a unique HTTPS hostname on the platform domain, shown in `public_url`
  and `default_public_url`. The slug is derived from `name`; if it is taken in the
  workspace, a short suffix is added.
- Private repositories need the RumptyCloud GitHub App. Send `git_provider: github_app`
  and `git_repo_full_name`. If GitHub is not connected, a `deploy_now` request fails with
  `Connect GitHub before deploying this repository.`
- For GitHub App repositories, a non-empty `root_directory` is checked against the branch
  and rejected if the folder does not exist.
- On a Free plan (`free_allowance_count` above `0`), scale-to-zero is forced on, the app
  runs a single replica, and the account's Free allowance must not be used up.
- A persistent volume pins the app to one replica. Preview apps need `git_provider` and no
  volume; otherwise `preview_apps_enabled` is silently turned off.
- `env_vars` are stored encrypted and are available both at build time and at runtime.
  `build_env` values are only passed to this first build and are not stored.
- `X-Idempotency` only deduplicates creates with `deploy_now: true`, where the key is
  stored on the build operation. The same key with a different `name` returns `409`
  (`action: idempotency_key_reused`). Without `deploy_now` nothing records the key, so a
  retry creates a second deployment (with a suffixed slug).

name.description: Display name. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. The slug and default hostname are derived from it.

plan_slug.description: Slug of a plan from [List deployment plans](/api/deployments/list-deployment-plans). Case-insensitive.

repo_url.description:
Git repository to build. Accepts `https://`, `http://`, `git://` and `ssh://git@`
URLs, or the `git@host:owner/repo.git` form. The path must look like
`/owner/repo`.

git_provider.description: Set to `github_app` to clone through your connected RumptyCloud GitHub App installation (needed for private repositories, previews and status checks). Omit for public repositories.

git_repo_full_name.description: `owner/repository` on GitHub. Required when `git_provider` is set. Each part may contain only letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`.

git_repo_id.description: GitHub's numeric repository ID, stored for reference.

root_directory.description: Folder inside the repository to build from, for monorepos. Must be relative and stay inside the repository. Empty or `.` builds from the root.

app_type.description: `service` for a long-running server, `static` for a static site. `backend` and `api` are accepted as `service`; `frontend` and `web` as `static`.

build_method.description: How to build the image. `railpack` detects the language and builds automatically. `dockerfile` uses the repository's Dockerfile.

build_command.description: Optional command that overrides the detected build step.

start_command.description: Optional command that overrides the detected start command.

health_check_path.description: HTTP path probed to decide the app is healthy. Must start with `/`, contain no whitespace and be at most 255 characters.

port.description: Port your app listens on. Zero or negative values use `8080`.

auto_deploy_enabled.description: Build and deploy automatically on every push to `branch` (GitHub App repositories).

security_scan_enabled.description: Scan each built image for known vulnerabilities. On unless you send `false`. Scanning is a paid add-on.

preview_apps_enabled.description: Create a temporary preview app for each pull request. Only applied when `git_provider` is set and there is no volume.

build_env.description: Extra variables for the first build only. Not stored. Ignored when `deploy_now` is `false`.

env_vars.description: Environment variables to store on the deployment. Keys must be unique.

volume_mount_path.description:
Absolute path to mount a persistent volume at. Send together with
`volume_size_gib`. Cannot be `/` or a system directory such as `/app`, `/etc`
or `/var` (use a subdirectory like `/var/data`), and cannot be under `/proc`,
`/sys` or `/dev`.

volume_size_gib.description: Volume size in GiB, from 1 to 512. Volumes are billed and can only grow later.

scale_to_zero_enabled.description: Let the app sleep after `scale_to_zero_idle_minutes` without traffic. It wakes on the next request. Always on for Free plans.

scale_to_zero_idle_minutes.description: Idle minutes before the app sleeps. `0` means the default of 5.

min_replicas.description: Instances that are always running. Must be `1` when scale-to-zero is on. `0` means the default.

max_replicas.description: Upper bound for autoscaling. Must be at least `min_replicas`, and `1` with a volume or on a Free plan. Each running replica is billed at the plan rate. `0` means the default.

target_request_rate.description: Requests per second per replica above which a replica is added. `0` means the default.

201.description: The deployment was created without a build (`deploy_now` was `false` or omitted). `operation_id` is empty and `status` is the deployment's status.

202.description: The deployment was created and its first build was queued (`deploy_now` was `true`).

400.description:
Validation failed. Possible messages include: `invalid request` (malformed JSON, or
`name`, `plan_slug` or `repo_url` missing), `name is required`,
`repo_url must be a valid git repository URL`, `repo_url must point to a git repository`,
`unsupported git provider`, `git_repo_full_name is required`,
`git_repo_full_name must look like owner/repository`, `root_directory must be relative`,
`app_type must be service or static`, `invalid build method`,
`health_check_path must start with /`, `volume size must be between 1 and 512 GiB`,
`invalid deployment plan`, `deployment plan is not available`,
`max_replicas must be between 1 and 5`,
`deployments with a persistent volume cannot scale beyond 1 replica`,
`the Free plan runs a single instance; switch to a paid plan to scale out`,
the Free app limit message, `duplicate environment variable <KEY>`,
`environment variable value is required`, a root directory not found on the branch, and
`Connect GitHub before deploying this repository.`

example.message: app_type must be service or static

428.description: You have not accepted the acceptable use policy yet.

example.message: acceptable use policy acceptance is required before creating a deployment

get.description:
Returns the workspace's deployments, newest first. Deleted deployments, pull request
previews and the component deployments of one-click [apps](/api/apps/list-apps) are not
included. Each item carries the status of its latest run in `last_run_status`, and
`display_status` shows `updating` while a new version builds for a live app.

Without query parameters, every deployment is returned in `data`. Send `page` or
`page_size` to paginate. A top-level `pagination` object is then added next to `data`, and
`q` filters the results. `q` is ignored unless `page` or `page_size` is present.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Values below 1 (or non-numbers) are treated as `1`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `10`. Values above `100` are capped at `100`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring search across name, slug, repository URL, branch, plan slug and status. Only applied when paginating.

200.description: The workspace's deployments. `pagination` is only present when `page` or `page_size` was sent.

get.description: Returns deployment counts for the workspace, using the same set of deployments as [List deployments](/api/deployments/list-deployments).

Returns how many Free plan apps the workspace owner's account may run, how many it runs now,
and how many are left. The allowance is per account, across every workspace the owner
owns. All values are `0` when no Free plan is offered.

Returns how many runs were started per day across the whole workspace, with how many
succeeded (`ready`) and failed. Only days with at least one run are included, oldest first.
Days are calendar dates in West Africa Time (UTC+1).

This counts every run in the workspace, including runs of pull request previews and of
one-click app components. For a single deployment, use
[List activity for a deployment](/api/deployments/list-activity-for-a-deployment).

Returns one deployment. Compared with the list, this also includes:

- `env_changes_pending` and `env_changes_require_build`, which tell you whether saved
  environment variable changes are waiting for the next deploy.
- `previews`, the live pull request previews of the deployment.

Component deployments of one-click apps can be read here too. They carry an `app_uid`.
Pull request previews themselves return `404`.

patch.description:
Changes a deployment's settings. Send only the fields you want to change.

Settings are saved immediately but most only take effect on the next build or deploy
(a [manual deploy](/api/deployments/deploy-a-deployment) or a git push). Changing
`artifact_retention` deletes older build images right away. Turning scale-to-zero off
wakes a sleeping (`idle`) deployment's status back to `active`.

Rules enforced:

- A persistent volume can be added, and its size can only grow. Once created it cannot be
  removed. A volume limits the app to one replica and is incompatible with preview apps.
- Scale-to-zero needs `min_replicas` of `1`. Free plans always scale to zero and run one
  replica, so sending `scale_to_zero_enabled: false` on a Free plan is rejected.
- Component deployments of one-click apps cannot scale to zero.
- Preview apps need a GitHub repository (`git_repo_full_name`).
- For GitHub App repositories, a changed `branch` or `root_directory` is checked against
  the repository.

To change the plan, use [Change a deployment plan](/api/deployments/change-a-deployment-plan).
The response is the updated deployment without `last_run_status`, so `display_status`
equals `status`.

branch.description: Branch to build. Cannot be empty.

root_directory.description: Folder inside the repository to build from. Must be relative and stay inside the repository. Empty builds from the root.

build_command.description: Build command override. Send an empty string to clear it.

start_command.description: Start command override. Send an empty string to clear it.

health_check_path.description: Health check path. Must start with `/`. Empty resets it to `/`.

port.description: Port your app listens on. Must be positive.

auto_deploy_enabled.description: Build and deploy automatically on every push to the branch.

preview_apps_enabled.description: Create a preview app for each pull request.

artifact_retention.description: How many built images to keep for rollbacks. `0` keeps all. The live image and in-flight runs are never pruned.

volume_mount_path.description: Absolute mount path of the persistent volume. Same rules as on create.

volume_size_gib.description: Volume size in GiB. Can only grow.

scale_to_zero_enabled.description: Let the app sleep when idle.

scale_to_zero_idle_minutes.description: Idle minutes before the app sleeps. `0` means 5.

target_request_rate.description: Requests per second per replica before scaling out.

400.description:
Validation failed. Examples: `invalid request`, `branch is required`,
`invalid port number`, `artifact_retention must be between 0 (keep all) and 50`,
`connect GitHub before enabling preview apps`,
`the persistent volume cannot be removed once created`,
`volume size can only grow: this deployment already has 10 GiB`,
`min_replicas cannot exceed max_replicas`,
`one-click apps cannot scale to zero; they stay always on`.

example.message: volume size can only grow: this deployment already has 10 GiB

delete.description:
Deletes the deployment. It is marked `deleted` straight away and disappears from listings,
billing stops, its custom domains are released and its pull request previews are removed.
Tearing down the running app, its route and its persistent volume (destructively) happens
in a `delete_deployment` operation.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

Component deployments of a one-click app cannot be deleted on their own. Delete the app
with [Delete an app](/api/apps/delete-an-app).

202.description: The deployment was marked deleted and the teardown was queued.

400.description: The deployment belongs to a one-click app.

example.message: this deployment is part of an app and can't be deleted on its own. Delete the app instead

get.description:
Returns how many runs this deployment started per day, with how many succeeded (`ready`)
and failed. Only days with at least one run are included, oldest first. Days are calendar
dates in West Africa Time (UTC+1).

post.description:
Queues a new build of the deployment's branch and rolls it out when the build succeeds.
Saved environment variable and settings changes are picked up. Any earlier build that is
still in progress is cancelled. While a live app rebuilds it keeps serving the current
version, and its `display_status` is `updating`.

The body is optional. Send no body, or `{}`, to build the latest commit on the branch.

For a component deployment of a one-click app (which runs a prebuilt image) the body is
ignored and this behaves like [Apply environment changes](/api/deployments/apply-environment-changes).

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id` and the new `run`.
See [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

commit_sha.description: Commit to build. Defaults to the head of the branch.

build_env.description: Extra variables for this build only. They override stored variables with the same key and are not saved.

400.description: `invalid request` (no or malformed JSON body), or `Connect GitHub before deploying this repository.`

post.description:
Rolls out the currently served image again without a rebuild, with the deployment's
current environment variables and runtime settings. A new run is recorded with the live
version's commit details.

Because environment variables are also available at build time, saved changes on a
deployment built from a repository need a rebuild. In that case (the deployment shows
`env_changes_require_build: true`) this endpoint returns `400` and you should use
[Deploy a deployment](/api/deployments/deploy-a-deployment) instead. One-click app
components run a prebuilt image, so for them this applies environment changes directly.

Past-due and suspended accounts get `402` with `action: past_due`. A retry with an
`X-Idempotency` key already used here still gets the original operation.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id` and the new `run`.
See [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

400.description:
Nothing is live yet (`Nothing is live yet. Deploy the app first — the initial deploy picks up all environment variables.`),
or the saved changes need a rebuild (`Environment changes apply on the next deploy. Use Redeploy.`).

example.message: Environment changes apply on the next deploy. Use Redeploy.

post.description:
Restarts the running version of the app without a build or a new run. If the platform
paused or stopped the app because it was unhealthy (see `crashloop`), this starts a
recovery attempt, and the `crashloop` state clears once the app reports ready.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). The response has no `run`.

crashloop.reason: The app kept crashing after it started.

400.description: Nothing has been deployed yet.

example.message: Nothing is live yet. Deploy the app first.

post.description:
Moves the deployment to another plan. Billing switches to the new rate immediately; usage
so far is settled at the old rate first.

- If the app has a live version, the current image is rolled out again under the new
  plan's CPU and memory limits, with no rebuild. A run and an operation are created and
  `status` is `queued`. See [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).
- Otherwise the plan is just recorded and the next deploy uses it. There is no
  `operation_id` and `status` is `completed`.

Both cases return `202 Accepted`. Moving to a Free plan turns scale-to-zero on and limits
the app to one replica; moving off a Free plan turns scale-to-zero off.

In the second case no operation is recorded, so the `X-Idempotency` key is not stored and
a retry returns `400` (`This deployment is already on the <plan> plan.`). Past-due and
suspended accounts get `402` with `action: past_due`.

plan_slug.description: Slug of the new plan from [List deployment plans](/api/deployments/list-deployment-plans). Case-insensitive.

202.description: The plan change was queued, or recorded immediately when nothing is live (`status` is `completed`).

400.description:
`invalid request` (missing `plan_slug`), `invalid deployment plan`,
`deployment plan is not available`, `This deployment is already on the Tiny plan.`,
`A build is in progress. Try again once it finishes.`,
`This deployment is managed by a one-click app and cannot change plans directly.`, or
the Free app limit message.

example.message: A build is in progress. Try again once it finishes.

get.description: Returns the custom domains attached to the deployment, with their verification status.

post.description:
Registers a custom domain for the deployment. The domain starts as `pending`. Nothing is
routed until you verify it.

To verify, create two DNS records at your DNS provider, then call
[Verify a custom domain](/api/deployments/verify-a-custom-domain):

- A `CNAME` record for the domain pointing to the host of the deployment's
  `default_public_url` (for example `acme-api.rumptycloud.app`).
- A `TXT` record at `rumpty-challenge.<domain_name>` whose value is the returned
  `verification_txt`.

Root (apex) domains such as `acme.com` are not supported yet. Use a subdomain such as
`www.acme.com`. A domain can only be registered once across RumptyCloud.

domain_name.description: Hostname to attach. Lowercased, trimmed and stripped of leading and trailing dots. Must be a hostname, not a URL.

201.description: The domain was added in `pending` state.

400.description: Validation failed: `invalid request`, `custom_domain must be a hostname, not a URL`, `custom_domain must be a valid domain name`, or the domain is a root domain.

example.message: root domains are not supported yet; use a subdomain such as www.acme.com

409.description: The domain is already registered.

post.description:
Checks the domain's DNS records against its authoritative nameserver and, if they match,
queues a `verify_custom_domain` operation that issues a TLS certificate and routes the
domain to the deployment. The domain stays `pending` until that operation finishes and
becomes `active`.

As soon as the checks pass, the deployment's `custom_domain` and `public_url` switch to
this domain. Environment variables that were seeded from the public URL (as one-click apps
do) are rewritten to the new domain and re-applied if the app is live.

If a DNS check fails, the domain is marked `failed` with the reason in `last_error`, and
the request returns `400` with the same message. The app must have been deployed first.

Calling this again is safe:

- If the domain is already `active`, you get `status: succeeded` with an empty
  `operation_id` and nothing is queued.
- If a verification queued in the last 15 minutes is still running, that operation is
  returned instead of a new one.

Otherwise this is asynchronous and returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

202.description: DNS checks passed and the routing operation was queued, or an existing result was returned.

400.description:
DNS verification failed, the domain is a root domain, or the app is not deployed yet
(`deploy the app before verifying a custom domain`,
`deployment does not have a default hostname yet`). Example DNS messages:
`CNAME record has not propagated or does not point to <hostname>`,
`verification TXT record not found or does not match: <verification_txt>`.

example.message: CNAME record has not propagated or does not point to acme-api.rumptycloud.app

delete.description:
Removes the custom domain. It disappears from
[List custom domains](/api/deployments/list-custom-domains) immediately, and its route is
torn down by a `delete_custom_domain` operation. If it was the deployment's primary
domain, `public_url` goes back to the platform hostname, and URL-derived environment
variables are rewritten and re-applied.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

202.description: The domain was removed and the route teardown was queued.

400.description: The app has never been deployed.

example.message: deploy the app before removing a custom domain

get.description:
Returns the deployment's environment variables, sorted by key. Values are never returned
here; `masked_value` is always `••••••••`. To read one value, use
[Reveal an environment variable](/api/deployments/reveal-an-environment-variable).

Requires a workspace role that can read secrets (viewers cannot).

put.description:
Creates the variable, or replaces its value if a variable with the same `key` exists. The
value is stored encrypted. Every variable is available both at build time and at runtime.

Changes are staged: the running app keeps its old environment until the next deploy, and
[Get a deployment](/api/deployments/get-a-deployment) reports `env_changes_pending: true`
until then. Apply them with [Deploy a deployment](/api/deployments/deploy-a-deployment).

Requires a workspace role that can manage secrets.

200.description: The saved variable, without its value.

400.description: `invalid request` (missing `key` or `value`), `key must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores`, `scope must be runtime or build`, or `value is required`.

example.message: key must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores

post.description:
Returns the **decrypted plaintext value** of one environment variable. Treat the response
as a secret: do not log it or store it in plain text.

Every call is recorded in the workspace audit log. Requires a workspace role that can
manage secrets.

200.description: The variable with its plaintext value.

delete.description:
Deletes the environment variable. If it is part of the running app's environment, the
removal is staged and takes effect on the next deploy, like any other change. Requires a
workspace role that can manage secrets.

The response is `200` even if no variable with this UID exists on the deployment.

get.description:
Returns the deployment's runs (builds and rollouts), newest first. `security_scan` carries
only the vulnerability counts here; get a single run for the full list.

Without query parameters, every run is returned. Send `page` or `page_size` to paginate;
a top-level `pagination` object is then added next to `data`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Runs per page. Defaults to `10`, capped at `100`. Sending this enables pagination.

200.description: The deployment's runs. `pagination` is only present when `page` or `page_size` was sent.

get.description: Returns one run, including the full vulnerability list of its security scan when there is one.

vulnerabilities.title: openssl: buffer over-read in X.509 parsing

get.description:
Returns all stored log lines of a run (build and rollout output), oldest first. Old log
lines are cleaned up after a retention period, so logs of old runs may be empty.

post.description:
Rolls the deployment back (or forward) to the image built by an earlier run, without
rebuilding. A new run is created with the source run's commit details and the current
environment variables and settings.

The source run must still have its build image (see `image_digest`), and it must not be
the version already being served. Images can be removed by `artifact_retention` or by
[Delete a run artifact](/api/deployments/delete-a-run-artifact).

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id` and the new `run`.
See [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

400.description: `This run does not have a deployable artifact.` or `This run is already serving the current app version.`

example.message: This run is already serving the current app version.

delete.description:
Deletes the container image built by a run to free storage. The run stays in the history,
but it can no longer be redeployed. If the run has no image, the run is returned
unchanged.

You cannot delete the image that is currently being served, or the image of the latest run
while it is still in progress.

200.description: The image was deleted. Returns the updated run, without `image_digest` and `artifact_size_bytes`.

400.description: `This artifact is serving the current app version.` or `This artifact belongs to an active deployment run.`

example.message: This artifact is serving the current app version.

get.description:
Returns the latest resource sample for the deployment: replicas, CPU, memory, network and
volume usage, summed across replicas. Percentages are relative to the plan's limits.

If no sample has been received yet, `available` is `false`, `unavailable_reason` explains
why, and only the limits are filled in. `stale` is `true` when the latest sample is more
than two minutes old.

Returns resource samples for the chosen time range, oldest first. At most the 2,000 most
recent samples in the range are returned. `step_seconds` is the suggested chart resolution
for the range; the points themselves are the raw samples.

When no samples exist in the range, `available` is `false`, `points` is empty and `latest`
is `null`.

400.description: `range` is not one of the allowed values.

get.description:
Returns HTTP traffic served through the deployment's public route over the chosen range:
request and 5xx error counts per time bucket, totals, the error rate and bytes in and
out. Traffic on the platform hostname and on all custom domains is added together.

When traffic data cannot be read (not available in this environment, the app has no public
route, or the metrics backend is temporarily down), the response is still `200` with
`available: false` and a reason in `unavailable_reason`.

400.description: `range` is not one of the allowed values.

get.description:
Returns the firewall policies attached to the deployment, with their rules and every
resource each policy is attached to. Inbound allow rules on public traffic are enforced at
the edge.

data.name: Office only
data.description: Allow HTTPS from the office network.

get.description:
Returns the catalog of enabled one-click app templates, sorted by name. Pass a template's
`slug` as `template` when you [create an app](/api/apps/create-an-app).

`from_monthly_cents` is the starting monthly price: the default web plan, each component's
pinned plan and the included persistent volumes.

data.name: WordPress
data.description: Launch a blog, business site, or online store in minutes. Your site comes with its own private database and durable storage.
data.setup_note: Open it now to finish the WordPress setup wizard (site title, admin account). Do this right away: the first visitor to an unconfigured site could claim it.

post.description:
Installs an app from a template. The app and all of its component deployments are created
at once and every component starts in parallel. The app's `status` moves from
`provisioning_database` (templates with backing services) or `provisioning_app` to
`active` once every component is ready, and `public_url` is then set.

If a component fails, the app becomes `failed` with the reason in `last_failure`, and the
components that were started are deleted, including their volumes, so nothing keeps
billing.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with the `operation_id` of the
`app_provision` operation, which is `running` from the start. Follow it with
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) or poll
[Get an app](/api/apps/get-an-app).

Things to know:

- You must accept the acceptable use policy first. Until then this endpoint returns `428`
  with `action: accept_acceptable_use_policy`.
- Each component is billed as its own deployment, plus its volume. Apps cannot use the
  Free plan, because they must stay always on.
- Component deployments are named after the app, with the template's suffix for backing
  services (for example `blog` and `blog-db`).
- Open the app soon after it is live and follow `setup_note`: many apps let the first
  visitor create the admin account.
- Send `X-Idempotency` to make retries safe. Repeating a create with the same key returns
  the original `app_provision` operation with `200 OK` and `is_replay: true`, and no second
  app is created. The key is checked before anything else, including the past-due check.
  Reusing it for a different action returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

template.description: Slug of an enabled template from [List app templates](/api/apps/list-app-templates). Case-insensitive.

name.description: Name of the app. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. The slug is derived from it, with a short suffix added if it is taken in the workspace.

plan_slug.description: Plan for the `web` component (and for any component without a pinned plan), from [List deployment plans](/api/deployments/list-deployment-plans). Defaults to the template's `default_plan_slug`. Free plans are rejected.

db_plan_slug.description: Plan for the primary database component (suffix `db`). Defaults to the template's `db_default_plan_slug`. Other backing services always use their pinned plan.

200.description: Replay. The `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a create, so the original `app_provision` operation is returned and nothing new is created. `status` is the operation's current status.

X-Idempotency-Completed.description: `true` when the original operation has already finished.

example.message: existing operation still in progress; not queued again

delete.description:
Deletes the app and all of its component deployments, **including their persistent
volumes and data**. The app and its components are marked deleted straight away (billing
stops and custom domains are released), and each component's runtime is torn down by its
own `delete_deployment` operation, web component first.

The response is `202 Accepted` with `status: deleted` and no `operation_id`. The
component operations are not returned; you can find them with
[List operations](/api/operations/list-operations). Because
the components are already deleted, they appear in the response with only `role` and
`deployment_uid`.

Concurrent deletes of the same app are serialized: while one is in progress, another
request returns `409` (`app deletion is already in progress`), unless it carries the same
`X-Idempotency` key, in which case it gets the first request's result.

Send `X-Idempotency` to make retries safe. The key is recorded when the delete starts,
so repeating the request with the same key returns `200 OK` with `is_replay: true`,
`is_completed: true` and `status: deleted` instead of `404`. On a replay the app is gone,
so `app` only carries `uid`, `name` and `status`. Reusing the key for a different action
or a different app returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

200.description: Replay. The app was already deleted with this `X-Idempotency` key, so nothing is done again.

example.message: existing operation already finished; not queued again

workspace. Open the URL in a browser while signed in to GitHub, choose the account or
organization and the repositories to grant, and confirm.

workspace and redirects to the RumptyCloud console at the `return_to` path. The URL carries
a signed `state` that is valid for **10 minutes**, so request a new one if it expires.

get.description:
Inspects a repository branch's file list and suggests how to build and run it: whether it
is a `static` site or a `service`, the framework, the root directory (for monorepos) and the
recommended build method. Only file names are inspected, not file contents.

How detection works:

- The repository root and common app folders (`apps/web`, `frontend`, `web`, `api`,
  `server`, `backend` and so on) are checked, along with every other folder. The best match
  wins.
- Framework config files are recognised first, for example Next.js, Nuxt, Remix and
  SvelteKit (`service`), and Astro, Gatsby, Angular and Vite (`static`). Then Go, Rust,
  Laravel, PHP, Rails, Ruby, Java, Elixir and Deno projects (`service`). Then generic
  markers: `package.json`, `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `index.php` and
  `index.html`.
- A `Dockerfile` in a folder makes `dockerfile` the recommended build method and sets
  `dockerfile_path`. `railpack` is always supported.

When nothing is recognised, `detected` is `false` and `recommended_build_method` is
omitted.

Requires the `secrets read` permission (owner, admin or developer role).

parameters.description: Repository in `owner/name` form. Must not contain spaces.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Branch to inspect. Defaults to `main`.

get.description:
Returns the database plans that are currently available, grouped by zone and sorted
cheapest first. Plans are per engine: use a plan whose `engine` matches the engine you
create. A plan with `monthly_price_cents` of `0` is a free plan and counts toward the
[free database quota](/api/databases/get-the-free-database-quota).

This endpoint is public and needs no API key or workspace.

Returns the engine versions you can create a database with, one entry per engine and
version. Pass `engine` and `version` from this list to
[Create a database](/api/databases/create-a-database).

Engines are `postgres`, `mysql` and `redis`. The `redis` engine runs Valkey, a
Redis-compatible server.

This endpoint is public and needs no API key or workspace.

Returns the workspace's databases, newest first. Deleted databases are not included, but
databases that are still `deleting` or that `failed` are.

Without query parameters, every database is returned in `data`. Send `page` or
`page_size` to paginate. A top-level `pagination` object is then added next to `data`,
and `q` filters the results. `q` is ignored unless `page` or `page_size` is present.

List responses never include the password. Use
[Get database credentials](/api/databases/get-database-credentials) for that.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Values below 1 (or non-numbers) are treated as `1`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `10`. Values above `100` are capped at `100`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring search across the database's name, slug, engine, version, host, status and display status. Only applied when paginating.

200.description: The workspace's databases. `pagination` is only present when `page` or `page_size` was sent.

post.description:
Queues a new database and returns `202 Accepted` with the `operation_id` of the create
operation. The database starts in `provisioning` and becomes `ready` when the operation
succeeds. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) or
[Get a database](/api/databases/get-a-database) to follow it.

**The response contains the generated password** in `database.password`, and in
`database.connection_string` and `database.internal_connection_string`. You can read it
again later with [Get database credentials](/api/databases/get-database-credentials).

Things to know:

- Pick `engine` and `version` from [List database versions](/api/databases/list-database-versions)
  and a `plan_slug` for the same engine from [List database plans](/api/databases/list-database-plans).
  `engine` is case-insensitive and `postgresql` is accepted as `postgres`.
- The engine's default user is created for you: `postgres` for PostgreSQL, `rumpty` for
  MySQL and `default` for Redis. For PostgreSQL and MySQL the database name is the name's
  slug with `-` replaced by `_` (for example `orders-db` becomes `orders_db`).
- PostgreSQL databases always get a public hostname on port `5432`. MySQL and Redis
  databases only get a public hostname when `public_access` is `true`. They are then
  reached on a dedicated port, returned as `public_port`. Public Redis connections use TLS
  (`rediss://`). Private databases are reachable only through `internal_host` from
  workloads running on RumptyCloud.
- Free plans (`monthly_price_cents` of `0`) are limited to 2 active databases per account,
  across every engine and workspace. Check [Get the free database quota](/api/databases/get-the-free-database-quota).
- Names are not required to be unique, but must contain at least one letter or digit.
- To create a database from a snapshot, send `snapshot_uid`. The engine, version and plan
  are then taken from the snapshot's source database (your `engine`, `version` and
  `plan_slug` are ignored), as are the database name and user. Storage is at least the
  source database's storage. Only snapshots of container-runtime databases can be used.

`X-Idempotency` is optional. If you repeat a create with a key you already used for a
database create, the original operation is returned with `200 OK`, `is_replay: true` and
the `X-Idempotency-Replay` header, and nothing new is queued. The replay is checked before
anything else (billing, validation, quota), so a retry still gets the original result.
The `name` is compared by slug: the same key with a different name returns `409` with
`action: idempotency_key_reused`, as does using the key for another action. A replay does
not include the password.

name.description: Display name of the database. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Its slug is used for the default database name.

engine.description: Database engine. Case-insensitive; `postgresql` is treated as `postgres`. `redis` runs Valkey. Required unless `snapshot_uid` is set.

version.description: Engine version from [List database versions](/api/databases/list-database-versions). Required unless `snapshot_uid` is set.

plan_slug.description: Slug of an available database plan for the same engine. Case-insensitive. Required unless `snapshot_uid` is set.

zone_slug.description: Optional zone. When set it must match the plan's zone, otherwise the request fails. The database always runs in the plan's zone.

public_access.description: Give a MySQL or Redis database a public hostname and port. PostgreSQL databases always get a public hostname; the value is still stored and returned.

snapshot_uid.description: UID of an `available` database snapshot in this workspace to create the database from. See the notes above.

`selected plan is not available for that database engine`,
`selected database plan is not available in that zone`, `invalid database version`,
`that database version isn't available yet`,
`database name must contain alphanumeric characters`, `invalid snapshot`,
`snapshot source plan is unavailable`, or
`create-from-snapshot is only supported for container-runtime database snapshots`.

403.description: You cannot create resources in this workspace, or the account already has the maximum number of free databases.

example.message: You've reached the limit of 2 free databases for your account. Delete one, or choose a paid plan to create another.

409.description: The snapshot is not `available` (`snapshot is not ready to restore`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: idempotency key was already used for a different operation; use a new X-Idempotency value

get.description:
Returns how many free-plan databases the account can still create. The limit is per
account (the workspace owner's account for workspace requests) and spans every engine
and workspace. Databases that are `failed` or deleted do not count.

Returns one database. The password is never included; `connection_string` and
`internal_connection_string` contain the user but no password. Use
[Get database credentials](/api/databases/get-database-credentials) to read it.

delete.description:
Queues deletion of the database and returns `202 Accepted`. The database moves to
`deleting` straight away and is removed from listings once the operation succeeds. If the
delete fails, the database moves to `failed`. Follow the operation with
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

All data is destroyed. The database's snapshots are kept: they are detached from the
database and can still be listed with [List database snapshots](/api/databases/list-database-snapshots),
used to create a new database, or deleted.

The database can be deleted in any status except already deleted. Without
`X-Idempotency`, each call queues a new delete operation until the database is gone. With
a key, a retry returns the original operation with `200 OK` and `is_replay: true`, even
after the database has been deleted (`database.status` is then `deleted`).

get.description:
**Returns secrets.** The response contains the database password in plain text and
connection strings with the password embedded. Treat it like the password itself: do
not log it or store it in plain text.

Requires the `secrets read` permission (owner, admin or developer role). Viewers get
`403`. Works in any status, including while the database is still provisioning.

`connection_string` is the public endpoint and is an empty string for a private MySQL or
Redis database. `internal_connection_string` only works from workloads running on
RumptyCloud. `ca_certificate` is the PEM certificate to verify the server's TLS
certificate (for example `sslrootcert` for PostgreSQL or `--cacert` for `redis-cli`).

After a successful [password rotation](/api/databases/rotate-the-database-password), this
returns the new password.

Lists the tables and views in a PostgreSQL or MySQL database, for use with
[Browse table rows](/api/databases/browse-table-rows). Redis databases have no tables;
use [List keys](/api/databases/list-keys) instead.

- PostgreSQL: tables, partitioned tables, views, materialized views and foreign tables
  in every schema except the system schemas, limited to those the database user can
  `SELECT`. Partitions are left out. Tables in `public` come first.
- MySQL: tables and views in every schema except `mysql`, `information_schema`,
  `performance_schema` and `sys`. Tables in the database's own schema come first.
- At most 2000 entries are returned.

The database must be `ready`. Data browser calls share a small platform-wide pool of
connections; when it is full you get `409` and should retry shortly. Requires the
`secrets read` permission (owner, admin or developer role).

400.description:
The request failed. Possible messages: `this database has no tables, browse its keys
instead` (Redis), `the data viewer doesn't support this database engine`,
`the database rejected the connection: <reason>`, or an error from the database.

example.message: this database has no tables, browse its keys instead

get.description:
Returns one page of rows from a PostgreSQL or MySQL table or view, as
`SELECT * FROM <schema>.<table> LIMIT <limit> OFFSET <offset>` in a read-only
transaction. Rows have no defined order.

`truncated` is `true` when more rows exist after this page (or when the response hit the
4 MiB size cap). The response shape and limits are the same as for
[Run a read-only query](/api/databases/run-a-read-only-query).

The database must be `ready`. Requires the `secrets read` permission (owner, admin or
developer role).

parameters.name: schema
parameters.description: Schema of the table, as returned by [List database tables](/api/databases/list-database-tables). For MySQL this is the database (schema) name.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: Name of the table or view. Quoted for you, so pass it exactly as listed.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to `50`. Values above `200` are capped at `200`. Zero, negative or non-numeric values use the default.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip. Defaults to `0`. Negative or non-numeric values are treated as `0`.

400.description: Validation or query failed. Possible messages: `schema and table are required`, `invalid table name`, `this database has no tables, browse its keys instead`, or the database's own error, such as a missing table.

post.description:
Runs **one** read-only statement against the database and returns the result as a grid.
Nothing you run here can change data.

**PostgreSQL**

- The statement runs in a `READ ONLY` transaction that is never committed, with
  `default_transaction_read_only` on. Writes (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, DDL and so on)
  fail with `400` and a message starting `the data viewer is read-only:`.
- Only a single statement is accepted. A string with several statements is rejected by
  the server.
- `statement_timeout` is 15 seconds and `lock_timeout` 3 seconds.
- Values are returned in PostgreSQL text format, and column `type` is the PostgreSQL type
  name (for example `int4`, `text`, `timestamptz`).

**MySQL**

- The session and transaction are read-only and multi-statement strings are not allowed.
  Writes fail with `400` and a message starting `the data viewer is read-only:`.
- `max_execution_time` is 15 seconds and lock waits time out after 3 seconds.
- Binary columns (`BINARY`, `VARBINARY`, `BLOB` types, `BIT`, `GEOMETRY`) are returned as
  `0x`-prefixed hex. Column `type` is the lower-case MySQL type name.

**Redis (Valkey)**

- `sql` holds one command line, split like `redis-cli` does: words separated by spaces,
  with `"double"` (supporting `\n`, `\t`, `\"` and `\xHH`) or `'single'` quotes.
- Only read-only commands are allowed: `PING`, `ECHO`, `TIME`, `DBSIZE`, `INFO`,
  `LASTSAVE`, `TYPE`, `EXISTS`, `TTL`, `PTTL`, `EXPIRETIME`, `PEXPIRETIME`, `SCAN`,
  `RANDOMKEY`, `OBJECT ENCODING|FREQ|IDLETIME|REFCOUNT|HELP`, `MEMORY USAGE|STATS|HELP`,
  `GET`, `MGET`, `STRLEN`, `GETRANGE`, `SUBSTR`, `LCS`, `GETBIT`, `BITCOUNT`, `BITPOS`,
  `BITFIELD_RO`, the read-only hash, list, set, sorted set and geo commands (`HGET`,
  `HGETALL`, `HSCAN`, `LRANGE`, `LLEN`, `SMEMBERS`, `SSCAN`, `ZRANGE`, `ZSCORE`, `ZSCAN`,
  `GEOSEARCH` and similar), `XRANGE`, `XREVRANGE`, `XLEN`, `XPENDING`,
  `XINFO STREAM|GROUPS|CONSUMERS|HELP` and `SORT_RO`. Anything else returns `400`.
- `db` selects the logical database, `0` to `15`.
- Replies are shaped into columns: `INFO` becomes `section`, `key`, `value`; `HGETALL`
  and `HSCAN` become `field`, `value`; `WITHSCORES` replies and `ZSCAN` become `member`,
  `score`; other arrays become `#`, `value`; single values become one `value` row. For
  `SCAN`-family commands, `command` is `next cursor <n>`. Nested arrays are returned as
  JSON strings. Column `type` is an empty string.
- The whole reply is capped at 8 MB. Larger replies fail with `400`; use a `SCAN` command
  or a narrower range.

**Limits for all engines**

- `sql` can be at most 64 KiB.
- At most 500 rows are returned. Results also stop once about 4 MiB of cell data has been
  read (SQL engines). When either cap is hit, `truncated` is `true`.
- Each cell is cut at 8 KiB, ending with `…`.
- `null` in `rows` means SQL `NULL` (or a nil Redis reply).
- The database must be `ready`, and data browser calls share a small platform-wide pool
  of connections (`409` when busy).

Requires the `secrets read` permission (owner, admin or developer role). Requests made with
an `mcp`-scoped API key (AI assistants) return `403` unless command access is turned on in
the workspace settings. The first 1000 characters of `sql` are recorded in the workspace
audit log.

sql.description: One SQL statement (PostgreSQL, MySQL) or one command line (Redis). Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.
sql.example: SELECT id, total_cents FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 2

db.description: Redis logical database to run the command against. Ignored for PostgreSQL and MySQL.

value.sql: SELECT id, total_cents FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 2

400.description:
The query was rejected or failed. Possible messages: `sql is required` (also sent for
malformed JSON), `query is too long`, `the data viewer is read-only: <reason>`,
`the query was cancelled because it took too long`,
`the command was cancelled because it took too long`,
`<COMMAND> isn't available in the data viewer, which only runs read-only commands`,
`unbalanced quotes in command`, `closing quote must be followed by a space`,
`command is required`, `db must be between 0 and 15`,
`the reply is larger than 8 MB, use a SCAN command or a narrower range`,
`the database rejected the connection: <reason>`, or the database's own error message
(PostgreSQL errors include the detail in brackets when there is one).

example.message: the data viewer is read-only: cannot execute DELETE in a read-only transaction

403.description: Your role cannot read secrets, or the request used an `mcp`-scoped API key and command access is turned off for the workspace.

example.message: running queries from AI assistants is turned off for this workspace; a workspace owner or admin can turn on command access in workspace settings

get.description:
Scans the keys of a Redis (Valkey) database with `SCAN` and returns their type and TTL.
Only available for Redis databases; other engines return `400`.

One call runs up to 20 `SCAN` rounds of 500 until at least 100 keys are found or the scan
completes, so a page can hold more or fewer than 100 keys. Keys in a page are sorted by
name. Pass the returned `cursor` back to continue; `"0"` means the whole keyspace has been
covered. As with any `SCAN`, a key may appear on more than one page.

Key names that are not valid UTF-8 are shown escaped in `key` and given exactly in
`raw_b64`. Use `raw_b64` with `key_b64` on [Get a key](/api/databases/get-a-key).

The database must be `ready`. Requires the `secrets read` permission (owner, admin or
developer role).

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Glob-style `MATCH` pattern. Defaults to `*`. At most 1024 characters.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous response. Omit (or send `0`) to start a new scan.

400.description: The request failed. Possible messages: `key browsing is only available for Valkey databases`, `pattern is too long`, `invalid cursor`, `db must be between 0 and 15`, or an error from the server.

example.message: key browsing is only available for Valkey databases

get.description:
Returns one key of a Redis (Valkey) database with its type, TTL, size and value. Only
available for Redis databases.

- `string`: `value` holds the first 64 KiB; `truncated` is `true` when the value is
  longer. `length` is the size in bytes.
- `hash`, `set`, `list`, `zset`, `stream`: `items` holds one page of about 200 entries
  and `length` is the element count. When there is more, pass `next` back as the `next`
  query parameter. `next` is an empty string on the last page.
  Columns are `field`, `value` (hash), `member` (set), `index`, `value` (list),
  `member`, `score` (zset) and `id`, `fields` (stream, with fields as a JSON object).
- Values that are not valid UTF-8 are shown with `\x` escapes. Each cell is cut at 8 KiB.

The database must be `ready`. Requires the `secrets read` permission (owner, admin or
developer role).

post.description:
Generates a new password for the database user and queues an operation that applies it
on the running database. Only PostgreSQL databases support rotation, and the database
must be `ready`.

Returns `202 Accepted` once the operation is queued. The response does not contain the
new password. The stored password switches only after the operation
succeeds; if it fails, the old password keeps working. Follow the operation with
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation), then read the new password with
[Get database credentials](/api/databases/get-database-credentials).

Rotation is a hard cutover: clients still using the old password fail when they next
reconnect.

Requires the `secrets manage` permission (owner, admin or developer role). `X-Idempotency`
is optional. A retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200 OK` and
`is_replay: true` instead of generating another password; the replay is checked before the
database's state, so it works after the rotation has finished.

400.description: The database engine does not support rotation (`password rotation is currently available for PostgreSQL databases only`).

example.message: password rotation is currently available for PostgreSQL databases only

post.description:
Moves the database to another plan of the same engine and returns `202 Accepted`. The
database must be `ready`. It switches to `provisioning`, is restarted with the new CPU and
memory, and returns to `ready` when the operation succeeds (or `failed` if it fails).
Follow it with [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

- Billing switches to the new plan's rate straight away. Usage up to now is charged at the
  old rate first.
- Storage only grows. If the new plan includes more storage, the disk grows to match. A
  plan with less included storage than the database already has is rejected.
- Expect a short interruption while the database restarts.

`X-Idempotency` is optional. A retry with the same key returns the original operation with
`200 OK` and `is_replay: true`, even once the resize has finished. The body is not
compared, so a retry with another `plan_slug` also returns the original resize.

plan_slug.description: Slug of an available plan for the database's engine. Case-insensitive. Must differ from the current plan.

202.description: The resize was queued. `database` already shows the new plan's size.

400.description:
Validation failed. Possible messages: `invalid request` (malformed JSON or missing
`plan_slug`), `plan_slug is required`, `invalid database plan`,
`selected plan is not available for this database engine`,
`This database is already on the <plan> plan.`, or the storage message
(`The <plan> plan includes <n> GiB of storage but this database already has <m> GiB provisioned. Choose a plan with at least <m> GiB of storage.`).

example.message: This database is already on the Seed plan.

get.description:
Returns the latest CPU, memory, disk and network sample for the database. The response
uses the same shape as VM metrics, so the database's UID is returned in `vm_uid`.

If no sample has arrived yet, `available` is `false`, the metric fields are left out and
`unavailable_reason` explains why. `stale` is `true` when the latest sample is more than
two minutes old.

200.description: The latest metrics sample. `vm_uid` is the database's UID.

get.description:
Returns a time series of the database's metrics over a time range. The response uses the
same shape as VM metrics, so the database's UID is returned in `vm_uid`. The step between
points depends on the range:

| `range` | `step_seconds` |
| ------- | -------------- |
| `15m`   | 15             |
| `1h`    | 60             |
| `6h`    | 300            |
| `24h`   | 900            |
| `7d`    | 3600           |
| `30d`   | 21600          |

If no samples exist in the range, `available` is `false` and `points` is empty.

parameters.description: Time window to return, ending now. Case-insensitive. Other values return `400` (`invalid metrics range`).

200.description: The metric history. `vm_uid` is the database's UID.

get.description:
Returns the firewall policies attached to the database, with their rules and every
resource each policy is attached to. Returns an empty list when no policy is attached.

data.name: Office only

get.description:
Returns the snapshots taken from this database, newest first, including ones still being
created or deleted. To also see snapshots of deleted databases, use
[List database snapshots](/api/databases/list-database-snapshots).

post.description:
Queues a point-in-time snapshot of the database's data volume and returns `202 Accepted`.
The snapshot is listed straight away with status `creating` and becomes `available` when
the operation succeeds. If the operation fails, the snapshot is removed. Follow it with
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

- The database must be `ready`.
- Only container-runtime databases support snapshots. Others return `400`.
- The new snapshot's UID is in `snapshot_uid`. The response's `name` is the
  **database's** name.
- Snapshots are kept when the database is deleted.

`X-Idempotency` is optional. A retry with the same key and the same `name` returns the
original operation with `200 OK`, before the database's state is checked. The same key with
a different `name`, or for a different database, returns `409`
(`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

400.description: Validation failed. Possible messages: `invalid request payload` (malformed JSON, or `name` missing or longer than 100 characters) and `snapshots are only supported for container-runtime databases`.

409.description: The database is not ready (`database must be ready before taking a snapshot`, `database is not available for snapshots`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: database must be ready before taking a snapshot

post.description:
Replaces the database's data with the contents of one of its snapshots and returns
`202 Accepted`. **Everything written since the snapshot is lost.**

The snapshot must belong to this database and be `available`, and the database must use
the container runtime. During the restore the database is `provisioning` and the snapshot
is `restoring`. When the operation succeeds the database is `ready` again. If it fails,
the database is marked `failed`. Follow it with
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation).

To restore into a new database instead, pass `snapshot_uid` to
[Create a database](/api/databases/create-a-database).

`X-Idempotency` is optional. A retry with the same key for the same snapshot returns the
original operation with `200 OK`, before the snapshot's state is checked.

400.description: The database does not support snapshots (`snapshots are only supported for container-runtime databases`).

example.message: snapshots are only supported for container-runtime databases

404.description: The database or the snapshot does not exist (`database not found`, `snapshot not found`).

409.description: The snapshot is not `available` (`snapshot is not in available state for restore`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: snapshot is not in available state for restore

Queues deletion of one of the database's snapshots and returns `202 Accepted`. The
snapshot moves to `deleting` and disappears when the operation succeeds. If it fails, the
snapshot goes back to `available`.

The database must still exist. For snapshots of deleted databases, use
[Delete a database snapshot](/api/databases/delete-a-database-snapshot).

`X-Idempotency` is optional. A retry with the same key for the same snapshot returns the
original operation with `200 OK`, even after the snapshot is gone. A replay's `name` is the
database's name, not the snapshot's.

404.description: The database or the snapshot does not exist (`database not found`, `snapshot not found`).

409.description: The snapshot is already being deleted (`snapshot is already being deleted`), or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

`database_uid` in the response is the snapshot's source database. On a replay it is empty
once the snapshot has been deleted.

get.description:
Returns the workspace's volumes, newest first. Deleted volumes are not included.

Without query parameters, every volume is returned in `data`. Send `page` or `page_size` to
paginate. A top-level `pagination` object is then added next to `data`, and `q` filters the
results. `q` is ignored unless `page` or `page_size` is present.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Values below 1 (or non-numbers) are treated as `1`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `10`. Values above `100` are capped at `100`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring search across the volume's name, slug, filesystem, attached VM UID and status. Only applied when paginating.

post.description:
Queues a new, unattached volume and returns `202 Accepted` with the `operation_id` of the
create operation. The volume starts in `creating` and becomes `available` when the
operation succeeds. Then [attach it](/api/volumes/attach-a-volume) to a VM.

Things to know:

- `size_gib` must be between 1 and 1024.
- Volume names do not have to be unique.
- A volume that is not yet marked `formatted` is formatted with its `filesystem` the first
  time it is attached.
- The `X-Idempotency` header is optional. If you repeat a request with a key already used for
  a volume create with the same name (compared by slug), the original operation is returned
  with `200 OK`, `is_replay: true` and the `X-Idempotency-Replay` header, and nothing new is
  queued. The same key with a different name returns `409`
  (`action: idempotency_key_reused`). The replay is checked before billing and
  validation, so a retry still gets the original operation after the account became past
  due.

name.description: Display name of the volume. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

description.description: Optional free-text description. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

size_gib.description: Size of the volume in GiB.

zone_slug.description: Zone to create the volume in. Case-insensitive. Defaults to `olas-closet`, currently the only zone. The volume can only be attached to VMs in the same zone.

filesystem.description: Filesystem to format the volume with. Case-insensitive.

format.description: Ask the provisioner to format the volume when it is created. Whatever you send, a volume that is not yet marked `formatted` is formatted on its first attach.

400.description:
Validation failed. Possible messages: `invalid request` (malformed JSON, or `name` or
`size_gib` missing or `0`), `name is required` (blank name),
`size_gib must be between 1 and 1024`, or `filesystem must be ext4 or xfs`.

409.description: The `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a different operation in the workspace (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

get.description:
Returns totals across the workspace's volumes. Volumes that are being deleted are not
counted.

Used space comes from the last filesystem usage reported by each VM's guest agent, so
volumes that have never been mounted count as empty.

200.description: Storage totals for the workspace's volumes.

get.description: Returns one volume, including the VM it is attached to and its latest reported disk usage.

delete.description:
Queues deletion of the volume and everything stored on it. The volume moves to `deleting`
straight away and disappears from listings once the operation finishes. If deletion fails,
the volume moves to `failed` and you can try again.

Detach the volume first. A volume that is attached, or being attached or detached, cannot be
deleted.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). The `X-Idempotency` header is
optional. A retry with the same key returns the original operation with `200 OK`, even
after the volume has been deleted (`volume.status` is then `deleted`). Without a key, a
retry returns `409` because the deletion is already in progress.

post.description:
Queues attaching an `available` volume to a VM. The volume moves to `attaching` straight
away and to `in-use` when the operation succeeds. If attaching fails, the volume goes back
to `available` and `last_failure` explains why.

Requirements:

- The volume must be `available`.
- The VM must be in this workspace, `running`, and in the same zone as the volume.

On its first attach, a volume that is not yet `formatted` is formatted with its
`filesystem`. Once the VM's guest agent reports the mounted filesystem, `device_name`,
`mount_path` and `usage` appear on the volume. Volumes are mounted under `/mnt/rumpty/`.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). The `X-Idempotency` header is
optional. A retry with the same key for the same volume returns the original operation with
`200 OK`, before the volume's state is checked. The same key with a different `vm_uid`
returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

vm_uid.description: UID of the VM to attach the volume to. See [List VMs](/api/virtual-machines/list-vms).

400.description:
The request is invalid or the volume or VM is in the wrong state. Possible messages:
`invalid request` (malformed JSON or missing `vm_uid`), `vm_uid is required`,
`volume is already attached; detach it first`, `volume is not available for attachment`,
`vm must be running to attach a volume`, or `volume and vm must be in the same zone`.

example.message: vm must be running to attach a volume

404.description: The volume or the VM does not exist in this workspace.

409.description: An attach is already in progress for this volume, or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: volume attach is already in progress

post.description:
Queues detaching an `in-use` volume from its VM. The volume moves to `detaching` straight
away and back to `available` when the operation succeeds. Its data is kept. If detaching
fails, the volume stays `in-use` and `last_failure` explains why.

Unmount the filesystem inside the VM first to avoid losing unwritten data.

This is asynchronous. It returns `202 Accepted` with an `operation_id`. See
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation). The `X-Idempotency` header is
optional. A retry with the same key for the same volume returns the original operation with
`200 OK`, before the volume's state is checked.

400.description: The volume is not attached to a VM.

404.description: The volume, or the VM it is attached to, no longer exists in this workspace.

409.description: A detach is already in progress for this volume, or the `X-Idempotency` key was used for a different operation (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).
