get.description:
Returns the current storage price sheet: the monthly price per GiB and the free allowance
for block volumes, snapshots, object storage (buckets) and build artifact storage.

This endpoint is public and needs no API key or workspace.

Returns how much storage your account uses across **all** your workspaces, split into file
storage (bucket objects) and build artifacts (deployment builds), compared with the free
allowance.

This endpoint is account-level, so it does not take an `X-Workspace-Slug` header. For a
single workspace's bucket usage, use
[Get workspace bucket usage](/api/buckets/get-workspace-bucket-usage).

Only objects whose upload has been completed (status `ready`) count towards usage.

Returns the workspace's buckets, newest first. Deleted buckets are not included, but
buckets that are still `provisioning`, `deleting` or `failed` are.

Without query parameters, every bucket is returned in `data`. Send `page` or `page_size` to
paginate. A top-level `pagination` object is then added next to `data`, and `q` filters the
results. `q` is ignored unless `page` or `page_size` is present.

Requires read access to the workspace (any role).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. Values below 1 (or non-numbers) are treated as `1`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `10`. Values above `100` are capped at `100`. Sending this enables pagination.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring search across the bucket's name, slug, storage bucket name, status and visibility. Only applied when paginating.

200.description: The workspace's buckets. `pagination` is only present when `page` or `page_size` was sent.

post.description:
Queues a new bucket and returns `202 Accepted` with the `operation_id` of the create
operation. The bucket starts in `provisioning` and moves to `ready` (or `failed`) when the
operation finishes. Poll [Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) or
[List buckets](/api/buckets/list-buckets) to see when it is `ready`. Uploads, access keys
and CORS changes are only accepted once the bucket is `ready`.

Things to know:

- Bucket names must be unique in the workspace. Uniqueness is checked on the slug of the
  name, so `Marketing Assets` and `marketing-assets` clash.
- `visibility` defaults to `public`. It cannot be changed after creation.
- The underlying S3 bucket name (`s3_bucket_name`) is generated for you from the workspace
  slug and the bucket's ID.
- Send `X-Idempotency` to make retries safe. Repeating a create with the same key returns
  the original operation with `200 OK` and `is_replay: true`, and no second bucket is
  created. The key is checked first, before the past-due check and validation. Reusing it
  for a different action returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.
- Past-due or suspended accounts cannot create buckets (`402`, `action: past_due`).

Requires the `resource write` permission (owner, admin or developer role).

name.description: Display name of the bucket. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Its slug must be unique among the workspace's buckets.

visibility.description: `public` serves objects from a public URL. `private` requires a signed URL to read objects. Case-insensitive.

400.description: Validation failed. Possible messages: `invalid request` (malformed JSON or missing `name`), `name is required` (blank after trimming), `visibility must be public or private`.

example.message: visibility must be public or private

409.description: A bucket with the same name (slug) already exists in this workspace, or the `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a different action (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

example.message: a bucket named "Marketing assets" already exists in this workspace

get.description:
Returns how many bytes the workspace's bucket objects use, compared with the account's free
file storage allowance, plus the maximum size of a single upload.

Only objects whose upload has been completed (status `ready`) are counted. The free
allowance is shared across all your workspaces. See
[Get account storage usage](/api/buckets/get-account-storage-usage) for the account-wide
total.

Requires read access to the workspace (any role).

delete.description:
Queues deletion of the bucket and returns `202 Accepted` with the `operation_id` of the
delete operation. The bucket moves to `deleting` straight away. Poll
[Get an operation](/api/operations/get-an-operation) to follow it.

When the operation succeeds, **every object in the bucket is deleted** and all of the
bucket's access keys are revoked. This cannot be undone. If deletion fails, the bucket's
status becomes `failed` and `last_failure` explains why.

Send `X-Idempotency` to make retries safe. The key is checked before the bucket's state, so
repeating a delete with the same key returns the original operation with `200 OK` and
`is_replay: true` instead of `409` or `404`. Reusing it for a different action or bucket
returns `409` with `action: idempotency_key_reused`.

The returned `bucket` omits `free_storage_bytes` and `max_image_size_bytes`.

Requires the `resource write` permission (owner, admin or developer role).

404.description: The bucket does not exist in this workspace or was already deleted.

409.description: The bucket is already being deleted, or the `X-Idempotency` key was already used for a different action or bucket (`action: idempotency_key_reused`).

put.description:
Replaces the browser origins allowed to make cross-origin (CORS) requests to the bucket,
for example so a web app can upload directly to a presigned URL or fetch objects with
`fetch()`. The RumptyCloud console's own origin is always allowed and is not listed.

The list you send replaces the current one. Send an empty array to remove all custom
origins. The change is saved immediately and pushed to storage. If that push fails, a
background sync applies it shortly afterwards.

Rules for each origin:

- Must be `scheme://host[:port]` with `https://` or `http://`, for example
  `https://app.example.com`. Paths, queries, fragments and credentials are rejected.
- `*` allows any site. A leading `*.` wildcard in the host (for example
  `https://*.example.com`) allows subdomains. `*` is not allowed anywhere else in the host.
- At most 255 characters each and at most 20 origins. Blank entries are ignored, and origins
  are lower-cased and de-duplicated.

The bucket must be `ready`. Requires the `resource write` permission (owner, admin or
developer role).

origins.description: The full list of allowed browser origins. Replaces the current list. An empty array or omitted field clears it.

200.description: The allowed origins were updated. Returns the bucket with the normalised `cors_origins`.

400.description:
An origin is invalid, or there are more than 20. Possible messages include
`"<origin>" needs https:// (or http://) at the start`,
`"<origin>" must start with https:// or http://`,
`"<origin>" should be just the scheme, host and port, e.g. https://app.example.com`,
`"<origin>" can only use * at the start of the host, e.g. https://*.example.com`,
`"<origin>" is too long`, `"<origin>" is not a valid origin, e.g. https://app.example.com`,
`a bucket can have at most 20 allowed origins` and `invalid request` (malformed JSON).

example.message: "www.acme.com" needs https:// (or http://) at the start

404.description: The bucket does not exist in this workspace.

409.description: The bucket is not `ready` yet.

example.message: allowed origins can be changed once the bucket is ready

get.description:
Returns every object in the bucket, newest first. Deleted objects are not included. Objects
whose upload has not been completed yet are listed with status `pending_upload`.

This endpoint is not paginated. For private buckets each object includes a freshly signed
`read_url` and its `read_url_expires_at`. For public buckets `read_url` is the public URL.

Objects written directly to the bucket with an S3 client (for example with a
[bucket access key](/api/buckets/create-a-bucket-access-key)) also appear here once storage
reports them.

Requires read access to the workspace (any role).

404.description: The bucket does not exist in this workspace.

post.description:
Starts an upload by reserving an object and returning a presigned URL to send the file to.
No file data goes through this endpoint.

**Upload flow:**

1. Call this endpoint with the file's name, content type and size. The object is created
   with status `pending_upload`.
2. Send the file's bytes with an HTTP `PUT` to `upload_url` (`method` is always `PUT`),
   setting **every header in `headers`** exactly as returned. For public buckets these
   include `x-amz-acl: public-read` and a `Cache-Control` header. The URL expires at
   `expires_at` (10 minutes by default).
3. Call [Complete an upload](/api/buckets/complete-an-upload) with `object_id` to mark the
   object `ready`. Only `ready` objects count towards storage usage and can be read with
   [Create an object read URL](/api/buckets/create-an-object-read-url).

```bash
curl -X PUT "$UPLOAD_URL" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/pdf" \
  -H "x-amz-acl: public-read" \
  -H "Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable" \
  --data-binary @report.pdf
```

The object's `key` is generated for you. It is the bucket's key prefix, then `key_prefix`
(if sent), then a slug of the file name with a short unique suffix, for example
`report-d5e6f7.pdf`.

Things to know:

- Allowed content types and extensions: `application/pdf` (`.pdf`), Word `.docx`
  (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`), `image/gif`,
  `image/jpeg` (`.jpg`, `.jpeg`), `image/png`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/webp`, `text/csv`,
  `text/html` (`.html`, `.htm`), `text/markdown` and `text/x-markdown` (`.md`), `text/plain`
  (`.txt`, `.md`, `.csv`), `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl` and `application/x-mpegurl`
  (`.m3u8`), `video/mp2t` (`.ts`), `video/mp4`, `video/quicktime` (`.mov`, `.qt`),
  `video/webm`, `video/x-matroska` (`.mkv`) and `video/x-msvideo` (`.avi`).
- If `filename` has an extension, it must match `content_type`.
- `size_bytes` must be above zero and no larger than the maximum upload size (1 GiB by
  default, shown as `max_upload_bytes` in
  [Get workspace bucket usage](/api/buckets/get-workspace-bucket-usage)).
- The upload is rejected with `403` if it would take your account's file storage past the
  free allowance.
- The bucket must be `ready`.

Requires the `resource write` permission (owner, admin or developer role).

filename.description: Original file name. Used for the object's `filename` and to build its key. Its extension must match `content_type`.

content_type.description: MIME type of the file. Case-insensitive. Must be one of the allowed types listed above.

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes. Must be above zero and within the maximum upload size.

key_prefix.description:
Optional folder path to place the object in, for example `invoices/2026`.
Leading and trailing slashes are ignored. Each folder name must start with a
letter or number and may contain only letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes and
underscores.

201.description: The object was reserved and a presigned upload URL was created.

400.description:
Validation failed. Possible messages: `invalid request` (malformed JSON or a missing
required field), `filename is required`, `size_bytes must be greater than zero`,
`file exceeds max upload size`, `unsupported file content_type`,
`filename extension does not match content_type`,
`filename must include a supported file extension`,
`folder path is too long (max 512 characters)` and
`folder names may only contain letters, numbers, spaces, dots, dashes, and underscores`.

The file is checked in storage first. If it is not there yet, the call fails with `409`

object stays `pending_upload`, so you can upload and complete again. The object's

creating the upload.

Completing an object that is already `ready` is safe and returns it unchanged. The storage
allowance is checked again here with the stored size. If completing the upload would take
your account past its free file storage, the call fails with `403` and the uploaded file
is removed from storage; the object stays `pending_upload`.

post.description:
Creates a firewall policy. The policy is not attached to anything yet, so it has no effect
until you [attach it](/api/firewall-policies/attach-a-firewall-policy) to a resource.

Every new policy starts with two default rules, so attaching it does not lock you out:

- TCP port `22` from `0.0.0.0/0` (SSH, needed by `rumpty ssh` and the CLI).
- TCP port `8080` from `0.0.0.0/0` (the default VM app port).

You can update or delete these rules like any other.

Policy names must be unique in the workspace. A name already used by another policy is
rejected with `409`. The check is on the exact name (after trimming spaces) and is
case-sensitive, so `Web servers` and `web servers` can both exist. Names of deleted
policies can be reused.

description.description: Optional free-text description. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

patch.description:
Changes a policy's name, description or default flag. Send only the fields you want to
change. Renaming the policy also changes its `slug`. This does not change any rules, so no
firewall operation is queued.

A name that another policy in the workspace already uses (exact, case-sensitive match) is
rejected with `409`.

name.description: New name. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Cannot be blank.

description.description: New description. Send an empty string to clear it.

is_default.description: Marks or unmarks the policy as a workspace default. This is a label only.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON (`invalid request`) or `name` is blank (`policy name cannot be empty`).

delete.description:
Deletes the policy, even if it is attached to resources. Its rules and all of its
attachments are deleted with it in one step, so the policy stops applying straight away and
no longer appears in any resource's policy list. A `firewall.apply` operation is queued for
every resource it was attached to, so their firewalls are rebuilt from their remaining
policies. A resource left with no policy is no longer filtered.

post.description:
Adds an allow rule to the policy and queues a `firewall.apply` operation for every resource
the policy is attached to. The response's `operation_id` is the first of those operations,
or an empty string when the policy is not attached to anything.

Defaults and limits:

- `direction` defaults to `inbound`, `action` to `allow` and `protocol` to `tcp`.
- Leave out both ports (or send `0` for both) to match all ports.
- Send only `port_start` to match a single port.
- `cidr` is required. A single address needs a prefix length, such as `198.51.100.7/32`.

direction.description: Traffic direction the rule applies to. Case-insensitive.

action.description: What to do with matching traffic. Only `allow` is supported.

port_start.description: First port of the range, from 1 to 65535. `0` together with `port_end` `0` (or both omitted) matches all ports.

port_end.description: Last port of the range. Defaults to `port_start`. Must not be lower than `port_start`.

cidr.description: Source address range in CIDR notation, IPv4 or IPv6. Use `0.0.0.0/0` to allow any IPv4 source.

description.description: Optional note about what the rule is for. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

patch.description:
Changes a rule. Send only the fields you want to change. Values are validated the same way
as in [Add a firewall rule](/api/firewall-policies/add-a-firewall-rule), and the policy's
default rules can be changed too.

If you send either port, the range is rebuilt from the ports in this request only: a missing
`port_end` becomes `port_start`, and a missing `port_start` is treated as `0`, which fails
validation. To change a range, send both `port_start` and `port_end`.

A `firewall.apply` operation is queued for every resource the policy is attached to. The
response's `operation_id` is the first of those, or an empty string when the policy is not
attached to anything.

direction.description: Traffic direction. An empty string means `inbound`.

protocol.description: IP protocol to match. An empty string means `tcp`.

port_start.description: First port of the range. See above for how ports are combined.

cidr.description: Source address range in CIDR notation. Cannot be blank.

description.description: New note. Send an empty string to clear it.

delete.description:
Deletes a rule from the policy, including the default SSH and app-port rules. A
`firewall.apply` operation is queued for every resource the policy is attached to, but its
ID is not returned.

Deleting the SSH rule from a policy attached to a VM can block `rumpty ssh` unless another
attached policy still allows port 22.

Attaching a policy that is already attached to the resource changes nothing. It returns
the existing attachment with `201` and an empty `operation_id`.
